definition_en: a written plan of action, a list or show, or a set of coded instructions; to arrange or write such instructions
core_image: 墙上贴着一张写满时间与步骤的纸，旁边的旧机器照着纸条上的指令一行行运行

sceneCN: 这里 program 指交给计算机执行的一整套指令（第 4 个义项：计算机程序）；句意：工程师载入程序，看着机器逐行执行。图中可辨识物件：墙上的时间表、纸条、旧机器、指示灯；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A plan of future action
senses.definition: a set of intended actions arranged in advance to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个目标而事先安排好的一系列行动
senses.example: The city launched a housing program for low-income families.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府启动了一项面向低收入家庭的住房计划。
senses.why: the Greek noun began as a public notice written down ahead of time, so the word still carries the idea of something laid out before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词最初指事先写好的公开通告，因此这个词始终带着「事情发生之前就摆好的安排」这一层意思。

senses.title: An order of events
senses.definition: a list showing the times and order of the parts of an event
senses.definitionCN: 列出活动各部分时间与顺序的清单
senses.example: The conference program lists every talk and the room it uses.
senses.exampleCN: 会议日程列出了每场报告及其所在房间。
senses.why: a written notice of what will happen and when is the most literal survival of the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 把「将发生什么、何时发生」写下来通告，正是原义最直接的延续。

senses.title: A printed list for an audience
senses.definition: the printed sheet given to an audience, naming the performers and the works
senses.definitionCN: 发给观众、写明演出者与曲目的印刷纸页
senses.example: She read the program before the orchestra tuned up.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团调音之前，她先读了节目单。
senses.why: theatres turned the order of a performance into a small printed booklet, and the booklet took the name of the order itself.
senses.whyCN: 剧院把演出顺序做成一本小册子，册子便直接沿用了「顺序」这个名字。

senses.title: A show that is broadcast
senses.definition: a single show or an ongoing series carried by a station
senses.definitionCN: 由电台或电视台播出的单个节目或系列节目
senses.example: The station dropped the program after one season.
senses.exampleCN: 电视台播出一季后停掉了这个节目。
senses.why: broadcasting inherited the word from theatre: each slot in the schedule is a program, whether or not paper is involved.
senses.whyCN: 广播沿用了剧院的说法：节目表上的每一个时段都叫一个节目，与纸张已无关系。

senses.title: Instructions a computer follows
senses.definition: an ordered set of coded instructions that makes a computer carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 使计算机完成一项任务的有序编码指令集合
senses.example: The program sorts the files by date and deletes the copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序按日期排序文件并删除重复副本。
senses.why: the earliest electronic machines were fed a written sequence of steps, exactly like a plan handed to a reader, so the plan word moved onto the machine.
senses.whyCN: 最早的电子机器接收的是一份写好的步骤序列，就像交给读者的一份计划，于是「计划」这个词就移到了机器上。

senses.title: A course of study
senses.definition: an organized course or set of courses leading to a qualification
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种资格的有组织课程或课程组合
senses.example: The new program leads to a master's degree in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新课程两年后可获硕士学位。
senses.why: schools borrowed the plan word because a degree is also a sequence of steps that a student is expected to complete in order.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了「计划」这个词，因为拿学位同样是一串要求学生按顺序完成的步骤。

senses.title: A government or agency scheme
senses.definition: an official scheme that organizes money and staff for a public purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为公共目的组织资金与人员的官方方案
senses.example: The literacy program trained teachers in three rural counties.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫盲计划在三个农村县培训了教师。
senses.why: public bodies write down what they intend to do and fund it, and that funded intention is called a program.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构把打算做的事写下来并拨款，这份带钱的打算就被称为项目。

senses.title: To set something to happen
senses.definition: to arrange for a device or system to act at a set time or in a set way
senses.definitionCN: 安排某个设备或系统在固定时间或以固定方式动作
senses.example: They programmed the lights to switch off at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把灯设定在午夜自动关闭。
senses.why: once a machine can hold its own sequence of steps, the verb means putting that sequence into it, even when no code is written by hand.
senses.whyCN: 一旦机器能自己保存步骤序列，动词就表示把序列装进去，哪怕并没有手写代码。

senses.title: To write instructions for a machine
senses.definition: to write the code that a computer or machine will execute
senses.definitionCN: 编写计算机或机器将要执行的代码
senses.example: He programmed the robot to pick only the ripe fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他给机器人编程，让它只摘成熟的果子。
senses.why: this is the modern verb built directly on the computing noun: the programmer writes the plan the machine will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接由计算机义名词转来的现代动词：程序员写下机器将要遵循的计划。

intro.en: Program is Greek in origin, Latin in transmission and French in form. Its oldest sense is a public notice written in advance; the computing sense is a twentieth-century extension. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: program 源于希腊语，经拉丁语传递，形式取自法语。它最古老的意思是事先写好的公开通告；计算机义是二十世纪的延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek programma meant a public written notice, built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write. The noun named a posted announcement, not a scheme of action.
items.cn: 希腊语 programma 指公开的书面通告，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。这个名词指的是张贴出来的公告，而不是行动计划。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma as a learned noun for a written notice or preface, keeping the Greek shape and the written, public flavour.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用 programma 作为书面通告或序言的学术名词，保留了希腊语的形式与「书面、公开」的色彩。

items.en: French programme entered English in the seventeenth century. English first used it for a public notice and soon for the printed order of a ceremony or performance.
items.cn: 法语 programme 在十七世纪进入英语。英语先用它指公开通告，很快又用它指仪式或演出的印刷顺序。

items.en: American printers shortened the ending to program. The two spellings now divide mainly by region, and the short form became standard in computing.
items.cn: 美国印刷者把词尾缩短为 program。两种拼写如今基本按地区分工，而短形式在计算机领域成为标准。

items.en: From the 1940s a program meant the coded sequence that drives a machine. The noun, and then the verb to program, followed the hardware into ordinary use.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，program 指驱动机器的编码序列。名词以及后来的动词「编程」随硬件一起进入日常使用。

items.en: The chain from Greek programma through Latin programma and French programme to English program is documented. Only the first written dates in English are approximate, and any Indo-European root proposed for graphein is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从希腊语 programma 经拉丁语 programma、法语 programme 到英语的这条链有文献依据，只是英语最早书证的年代为约数；为 graphein 提出的印欧语词根属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

note.en: The first group is the same word in other shapes and roles; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a plan, a timetable and software.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的其他形式与角色；第二组是与计划、时间表和软件相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun, and the usual form for a printed list of performances; computing writing prefers program everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写，也是节目单的常用形式；计算机写作各地多用 program。

entries.definition: The activity of writing code, not the code of one task; the noun names the work, while program names the product.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写代码这项活动，而不是某一任务的代码；名词指工作，program 指成品。

entries.definition: The person who writes the code; it answers who, where program answers what.
entries.definitionCN: 指写代码的人；它回答「谁」，而 program 回答「什么」。

entries.definition: Built on the Greek noun with a Latinised ending: it describes something done by fixed plan, as in programmatic music or programmatic reform.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊名词加拉丁化词尾构成：描述按固定计划进行的事物，如标题音乐或按纲领推行的改革。

entries.definition: The broad intention and the steps meant to reach it; a program is usually a plan that has been written down, funded or scheduled.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体意图及实现它的步骤；program 通常是已写下来、已拨款或已排期的计划。

entries.definition: The arrangement of times and dates; a program may contain a schedule, but a schedule says only when, not what for.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间与日期的安排；program 里可能含 schedule，但时间表只说「何时」，不说「为何」。

entries.definition: Programs and data treated as a product or a body of material; one program is a single unit of software.
entries.definitionCN: 把程序与数据当作产品与整套材料；一个 program 是软件的一个单元。

entries.definition: The list of items to be discussed at a meeting; it is a program for a discussion rather than for a machine or a season.
entries.definitionCN: 会议上要讨论的事项清单；它是讨论的程序，而非机器或演出季的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek pro- means before and graphein means write, so a program is something written down before it happens.
normal.cn: 希腊语 pro- 意为「在前」，graphein 意为「书写」，所以 program 就是事先写下来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs program, programme, programming, programmer, programmable and programmatic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programme、programming、programmer、programmable 与 programmatic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the plan sense: training program, welfare program, housing program.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示「计划」义：培训计划、福利计划、住房计划。

normal.en: The two spellings differ only in the ending, and computing settles on program everywhere.
normal.cn: 两种拼写只差词尾，计算机领域各地都落在 program 上。

normal.en: The verb splits by object: you program a computer with code, and you program a timer with a setting.
normal.cn: 动词按宾语分工：给计算机编程是写代码，给定时器设程序是调设定。

abstract.en: Picture a playbill that keeps fluttering after the audience has gone, still deciding the order of a night that is over.
abstract.cn: 想象一张观众散场后仍在飘动的节目单，还在决定一个已经结束的夜晚的顺序。

abstract.en: Picture a strip of paper sliding into a machine, and the machine growing a spine as it reads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条滑进机器，机器一边读一边长出脊骨。

abstract.en: Picture traffic lights blinking to a timetable nobody in the street can see.
abstract.cn: 想象街上的红绿灯按一张路人看不见的时间表眨眼。

examples.en: A well-written program can be read by another person without running it.
examples.cn: 写得好的程序，别人不运行也能读懂。

examples.en: The museum program lists four lectures and one concert.
examples.cn: 博物馆的活动日程列出四场讲座和一场音乐会。

examples.en: She programmed the irrigation system to water the field before dawn.
examples.cn: 她把灌溉系统设定在黎明前浇水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来个（gram）」——事先扑上去写下来的东西，就是计划与程序

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma「公开书面通告」→ 拉丁 programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；计算机义始于二十世纪四十年代。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one thread: something is written down in advance, first as a notice, then as an order of events, a printed list, a show, a set of machine instructions, a course, a funded scheme, and at last as the act of setting or coding.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一条线索展开：某事被事先写下来，先是通告，再是活动顺序、印刷节目单、播出节目、机器指令集、课程、拨款项目，最后是设定与编程这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of times and steps pinned to the wall, with a machine reading the sheet line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满时间与步骤的纸钉在墙上，机器一行行读着这张纸。

branches.en: PLAN AND SCHEME: an intention set down in advance, whether a household plan or a funded public scheme.
branches.cn: 计划与方案：事先写下的意图，无论家务安排还是拨款推行的公共项目。

branches.en: TIME ARRANGEMENT: an order of events in time, applied to people and then to devices that must act on cue.
branches.cn: 时间安排：按时间排出的活动顺序，先用于人，后用于必须按时动作的设备。

branches.en: LIST AND SHOW: the printed order becomes a booklet, and the booklet gives its name to the broadcast item.
branches.cn: 节目单与节目：印刷的顺序成为小册子，小册子又把名字让给播出的节目。

branches.en: CODE: the written sequence is now for a machine, first as a noun and then as the verb that puts it there.
branches.cn: 代码：写下的序列改为给机器用，先是名词，再是把序列装进去的动词。

branches.en: COURSE OF STUDY: a degree is also a sequence of steps completed in order, so schools use the same word.
branches.cn: 课程：学位同样是一串按顺序完成的步骤，学校于是沿用同一个词。

intro.en: Program is Greek in its two pieces, Latin in its noun ending and French in its modern shape. English then added -ing, -er and -able to build the computing family.
intro.cn: program 的两个构件来自希腊语，名词词尾来自拉丁语，现代形式来自法语。英语随后加 -ing、-er、-able 构成计算机词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin programma is the one learned borrowing that carries the word from Greek into French and English; the other Latin-looking ending -atic came later through French adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 programma 是把这个词从希腊语带到法语与英语的唯一学术借词；另一个似拉丁的词尾 -atic 是后来经法语形容词进入的。

items.example: The prefix places the writing ahead of the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「写」放在事情发生之前。

items.example: The verb names the act of setting marks down.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把符号落下来的动作。

items.example: The ending turns the act of writing into a written thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「写」这个动作变成「写出来的东西」。

items.example: The Greek noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的源头。

items.meaning: a notice; an order of events
items.example: English took the French shape in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪接受了法语的形式。

items.meaning: a plan or a coded instruction set
items.example: The short spelling became standard in computing.
items.exampleCN: 短拼写在计算机领域成为标准。

items.example: Programming names the work rather than the product.
items.exampleCN: programming 指这项工作，而不是成品。

items.example: A programmer is the one who writes the code.
items.exampleCN: programmer 就是写代码的人。

items.example: A programmable device can hold a new sequence.
items.exampleCN: 可编程设备能装入新的序列。

items.example: Programmatic music follows a written story.
items.exampleCN: 标题音乐遵循一个写好的故事。

definition_zh: 与……形成鲜明对照；与……截然相反，用来突出两者的对立或差别
definition_en: used to introduce a thing that differs sharply from the one just mentioned or from what would be expected
core_image: 同一张展台上左边满杯、右边空杯，两束灯光的颜色正好相反
scene: 展台两侧并排放着满杯与空杯，标签特意标出两者的差别。 In contrast to the first case, the second case held an empty cup.
sceneCN: 这里指第二个展柜与第一个恰好相反（第 1 个义项：与……形成鲜明对照）；句意为与第一个展柜不同，第二个展柜里是空杯。图中可辨识物件：展台、满杯、空杯、两束灯光。

状语短语：相比之下

collocations.phrase: in contrast to the situation elsewhere

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「对立而站」一系经意大利语、法语而来，义为「对照；形成对比」
由该名词加「有……性质」的形容词尾构成，义为「对比的」

由介词加名词构成的独立连接语，义为「相比之下」
由动词加介词构成，义为「与……形成对比」

senses.title: A sharp opposition
senses.definition: used to set a thing against another that is sharply different
senses.definitionCN: 把一物与另一明显不同之物并置
senses.example: In contrast to the coastal towns, the inland villages lost population.
senses.exampleCN: 与沿海城镇相反，内陆村庄人口减少。
senses.why: The preposition names the second term, and the sentence asserts a difference rather than a shared measure.
senses.whyCN: 介词点出第二项，句子断言的是差异而不是共同的尺度。

senses.title: The fronted frame
senses.definition: placed at the front of a clause to announce that the opposite case follows
senses.definitionCN: 置于从句开头，宣告接下来是相反的情形
senses.example: In contrast to the north, the south relies on service industries.
senses.exampleCN: 与北方相反，南方依靠服务业。
senses.why: Fronting makes the contrast structural: the reader knows the second half will mirror, then reverse, the first.
senses.whyCN: 前置让对照成为结构性的：读者知道后半句先对应、后反转前半句。

senses.title: Against expectation
senses.titleCN: 与预期或普遍看法相反
senses.definition: used to correct an assumption that the reader is likely to hold
senses.definitionCN: 用来纠正读者可能持有的假设
senses.example: In contrast to popular belief, the desert supports a rich microbial life.
senses.exampleCN: 与普遍看法相反，沙漠里生活着丰富的微生物。
senses.why: Here the first term is not a fact but a belief, so the phrase does the work of a correction.
senses.whyCN: 这里的第一项不是事实而是看法，短语因此承担纠正的功能。

senses.title: Against the evidence
senses.definition: used in research writing to introduce a result that opposes an earlier one
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中引出与先前结果相反的结果
senses.example: In contrast to the earlier trial, the second trial found no benefit.
senses.exampleCN: 与早先的试验相反，第二次试验没有发现益处。
senses.why: Research prose needs to mark disagreement without calling the earlier work wrong, and this frame does exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 研究写作需要标出分歧又不判定早先工作错误，这一框架正好做到。

senses.title: A difference in kind
senses.definition: used when two things differ in nature rather than in degree
senses.definitionCN: 两者在性质上不同，而非程度不同
senses.example: In contrast to a loan, a grant never has to be repaid.
senses.exampleCN: 与贷款不同，赠款从不需要偿还。
senses.why: When the difference is categorical, contrast is the right tool and comparison would understate it.
senses.whyCN: 差异是类别性的时候，对照才合适，比较会低估它。

senses.title: Syntactic division of labour
senses.definition: used with a following noun, where by contrast would stand alone
senses.definitionCN: 后面接名词，而独立连接语则单独使用
senses.example: In contrast to the first group, the second group met every target.
senses.exampleCN: 与第一组相反，第二组达成了全部目标。
senses.why: The two forms split the work: this one takes a benchmark, while by contrast takes none.
senses.whyCN: 两种形式分工：这一个带基准，另一个不带。

senses.title: Graded sharpness
senses.definition: used with sharp or marked to raise the force of the difference
senses.definitionCN: 与「鲜明的」「显著的」一类词连用以提高差异的力度
senses.example: In contrast to last year, sales fell in every region, a sharp reversal.
senses.exampleCN: 与去年相反，各地销量都下降了，形成鲜明反转。
senses.why: The modifier sits inside the phrase, so force is added without changing the frame.
senses.whyCN: 修饰语插在短语内部，力度增强而框架不变。

senses.title: Parallel-structure contrast
senses.definition: used to balance two opposite statements in one sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在同一句中平衡两个相反的陈述
senses.example: In contrast to the north, where prices rose, the south saw prices fall.
senses.exampleCN: 与物价上涨的北方相反，南方物价下跌。
senses.why: Parallel wording makes the reversal measurable; the phrase marks where the second half begins.
senses.whyCN: 平行措辞让反转可衡量，短语标出后半句的起点。

intro.en: Contrast came into English through French from Italian contrastare, a verb reconstructed in Vulgar Latin from Latin contra, against, and stare, to stand. The reconstruction is reliable; the date of the English phrase is approximate.
intro.cn: contrast 经法语、意大利语进入英语，其动词是通俗拉丁语中由 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」构成的重构形式。该重构可靠；英语短语的年代为约数。

items.en: Contra means against and appears in contradiction and contraflow.
items.cn: contra 意为「反对」，也出现在 contradiction 与 contraflow 中。

items.en: Stare means to stand, giving the picture of two things standing face to face.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立」，画出两物面对面站立的画面。

items.en: The reconstructed verb meant to stand against or withstand.
items.cn: 重构动词意为「对立而站、抵抗」。

items.en: Italian contrastare passed into French as contraster and then into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 意大利语 contrastare 传入法语作 contraster，十六世纪再进入英语。

items.en: The prepositional frame belongs to modern written English; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 这一介词框架属近代书面英语，确切首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the contrast slot with different prepositions or functions; the second group holds other ways of marking opposition.
note.cn: 第一组占同一对照位置，但介词或功能不同；第二组是其他标记对立的方式。

entries.definition: With is the older and more bookish partner of to, with the same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: with 是 to 更旧、更书面的搭档，意义相同。

entries.definition: It weighs two items on one scale rather than declaring them opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 它把两项放在同一尺度上称量，而非宣告对立。

entries.definition: It works alone between clauses and takes no noun after it.
entries.definitionCN: 它独立用于句间，后面不接名词。

entries.definition: It rejects a stated negative claim; contrast merely sets two facts side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 它否定被说出的否定命题；对照只把两件事并置。

entries.definition: It simply names the different item, with no signal of rhetorical weight.
entries.definitionCN: 它只点出不同之物，不带修辞力度的信号。

entries.definition: It joins two full clauses that differ, common in formal and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 它连接两个不同的完整从句，多见于正式与法律文本。

entries.definition: It separates two options and usually implies a preference.
entries.definitionCN: 它把两个选项分开，通常暗示偏好。

entries.definition: It marks the reverse side of a relation rather than a plain difference.
entries.definitionCN: 它标出关系的反面，而非单纯差异。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real Latin pair, the real prepositions and the contrast-comparison split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实拉丁语对、真实介词以及对照与比较的分工。

normal.en: Contra is against and stare is to stand, so the two things stand face to face.
normal.cn: 词根一是「反」、一是「站」，两物便面对面站着。

normal.en: To takes a noun; by contrast stands alone.
normal.cn: 带介词的形式接名词，独立形式单独使用。

normal.en: At the front it announces the other side; mid-sentence it pivots.
normal.cn: 句首宣告另一面，句中完成转折。

normal.en: Sharp and marked go inside the phrase to raise the force.
normal.cn: 表示「鲜明」「显著」的词插在短语内部增强力度。

normal.en: Contrast opposes; comparison weighs. Mixing them weakens both.
normal.cn: 对照管对立，比较管称量，混用会削弱两者。

abstract.en: Like two lamps of opposite colours lit at the two ends of one table.
abstract.cn: 像同一张桌子两端亮起两盏颜色相反的灯。

abstract.en: Like a hinge in the middle of a sentence, letting the second half swing the other way.
abstract.cn: 像句子中间的一枚铰链，让后半句向另一边转。

abstract.en: Like a scale with one full pan and one empty pan, both visible at once.
abstract.cn: 像一架天平，一端满一端空，同时可见。

examples.en: In contrast to the earlier model, the new model runs on a single battery.
examples.cn: 与早先的型号相反，新机型只靠一节电池运行。

examples.en: In contrast to the coastal group, the inland group moved less.
examples.cn: 与沿海组相反，内陆组流动更少。

examples.en: In contrast to last winter, this winter has been mild.
examples.cn: 与去年冬天相反，今年冬天一直温和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因 康特拉斯特 图」——满杯与空杯并排摆着，灯光颜色正好相反：与……形成对照

root: contrast 经法语、意大利语进入英语，其动词由拉丁语 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」构成通俗拉丁语重构形式；该介词框架属近代书面英语，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by what is being opposed: another fact, a fronted opposite case, an expectation, earlier evidence, a different kind, a syntactic partner, a graded difference and a parallel clause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按对立对象区分：另一事实、前置相反情形、预期、早先证据、不同类别、句法搭档、分级差异、平行从句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one full cup and one empty cup under two lights of opposite colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：满杯与空杯摆在两束相反颜色的灯光下。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: the second clause mirrors the first and then reverses it.
branches.cn: 镜像：后半句先对应前半句，再反转。

branches.en: THE CORRECTION: the first term is a belief, so the phrase sets the record straight.
branches.cn: 纠正：第一项是看法，短语借此澄清事实。

branches.en: THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE: research uses it to mark disagreement without blame.
branches.cn: 反证：研究用它标出分歧而不追责。

branches.en: THE CATEGORICAL GAP: two kinds or two parallel clauses are set apart.
branches.cn: 类别落差：两个类别或两个平行从句被分开。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND ITS FORCE: a following noun, plus sharp or marked inside.
branches.cn: 框架与力度：后接名词，内部可加「鲜明」「显著」。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin preposition of opposition to a Latin verb of standing; the verb reached English through Italian and French.
intro.cn: 短语把表对立的拉丁介词与表站立的拉丁动词结合起来；动词经意大利语、法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are contra, against, and stare, to stand; contrastare is the reconstructed Vulgar Latin link.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」；contrastare 是通俗拉丁语的重构环节。

items.example: Contra appears in many English compounds of opposition.
items.exampleCN: 这个词出现在许多表对立的英语复合词里。

items.example: The verb supplies the image of standing one's ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「站定不退」的画面。

items.example: The reconstructed verb links Latin to Italian.
items.exampleCN: 重构动词把拉丁语与意大利语接上。

items.example: French carried the verb into English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 法语在十六世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.example: The noun names the difference that the phrase points to.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名短语所指出的差异。

items.example: Linguistics speaks of contrastive pairs.
items.exampleCN: 语言学讲「对比对」。

items.example: The phrase takes a noun as its benchmark.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语以名词作基准。

items.example: Its twin usually stands alone between sentences.
items.exampleCN: 它的双胞胎通常在句间独立使用。

definition_zh: 绘画；油画；画作；（上漆的）涂装
definition_en: the art or activity of making pictures with paint, a picture made in this way, or the act of coating a surface with paint
core_image: 一支笔蘸着湿颜料在布上走过，留下一条再也改不回原样的痕迹
scene: 展厅里，修复师在斜射灯下检查一幅画的裂纹，判断清漆是否该去掉。 The conservator examined the painting under raking light.
sceneCN: 这里 painting 指「一幅画作」（第 1 个义项：用颜料绘成的图画）；句意为修复师在斜射光下检查这幅画，判断裂纹与清漆状况。

pos.zh: 绘画（艺术或活动）；画作；涂装

derivatives.zh: paint + -er（人）→ 画家／油漆工；从「动作」转到「施事者」
paint + -ed（过去分词）→ 涂过漆的；从「动作」转到「状态」
paint + work（成品）→ 漆面；从「涂料」转到「涂装结果」
painter + -ly（形容词）→ 有绘画笔触感的；从「人」转到「画面质感」

senses.title: A painted picture
senses.definition: a picture made with paint, especially on canvas or panel
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料绘成的图画，尤指画在布面或木板上
senses.example: The conservator examined the painting under raking light.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师在斜射光下检查这幅画。
senses.why: The noun of result names the finished object: what the verb paint produces, treated as a thing that can hang on a wall.
senses.whyCN: 结果名词命名完成的物件：动词 paint 所产出之物，被当作可以挂上墙的东西。

senses.title: The art form
senses.definition: the art of making pictures with paint, considered as a discipline
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料作画的艺术，作为一门学科来看
senses.example: Painting is older than photography by many centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 绘画比摄影早了许多个世纪。
senses.why: The same result-noun can name the whole practice, because a body of works defines a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 同一个结果名词也能命名整个实践，因为一批作品就界定了一门学科。

senses.title: The act of painting
senses.definition: the activity or process of making a picture with paint
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料制作图画的行动或过程
senses.example: Painting takes patience before it takes skill.
senses.exampleCN: 作画先要耐心，然后才谈技巧。
senses.why: The verbal noun also names the ongoing action, not only its outcome; English -ing forms routinely hold both readings.
senses.whyCN: 动名词也命名进行中的动作，而不只是结果；英语 -ing 形式通常同时容纳两种读法。

senses.title: A school or period style
senses.definition: the characteristic style of a school, region or period
senses.definitionCN: 某个画派、地区或时期的典型风格
senses.example: Dutch painting of the golden age is full of reflected light.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金时代的荷兰绘画充满反射光。
senses.why: A mass of works made in one place and time shows shared habits, so the noun can name a style rather than one picture.
senses.whyCN: 一地一时的大量作品显出共同习惯，因此这个名词能命名一种风格，而非一幅画。

senses.title: A subject category
senses.definition: a genre defined by subject, as in portrait painting or landscape painting
senses.definitionCN: 按题材界定的画类，如肖像画或风景画
senses.example: Portrait painting paid better than landscape in his day.
senses.exampleCN: 在他那个年代，肖像画比风景画更赚钱。
senses.why: Genres are compounds built on the noun: the subject in front narrows the art form to one marketable kind.
senses.whyCN: 画类是以这个名词构成的复合词：前面的题材把艺术门类收窄为一种可售卖的类别。

senses.title: Paintwork on a surface
senses.definition: the coating of paint on a building or object
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或物件表面的涂料层
senses.example: The painting of the bridge takes six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的涂装要六周。
senses.why: Because the verb also means 'coat a surface', the noun can name the layer applied, not a picture at all.
senses.whyCN: 因为动词也指「涂覆表面」，名词便能命名所涂的层，与图画无关。

senses.title: The coating trade
senses.definition: the trade or industry of applying paint to surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 把涂料施于表面的行业
senses.example: Industrial painting moved to the new shed.
senses.exampleCN: 工业涂装搬到了新厂房。
senses.why: An activity repeated for hire becomes an industry, so the -ing noun names the trade as well as the act.
senses.whyCN: 为报酬反复进行的活动会变成行业，因此 -ing 名词既命名动作，也命名行业。

senses.title: A medium or technique
senses.definition: a particular medium or technique, as in oil painting or watercolour painting
senses.definitionCN: 某种特定媒介或技法，如油画或水彩画
senses.example: She works in oil painting but teaches drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 她画油画，但教的是素描。
senses.why: The medium in front of the noun turns the art form into a technique: what the paint is made of changes how the picture is made.
senses.whyCN: 名词前的媒介把艺术门类变成一种技法：颜料由什么构成，改变了画如何被制作。

intro.en: Painting is the verbal noun of paint, recorded around 1200; paint came through Old French from Latin pingere, whose deeper root is reconstructed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: painting 是 paint 的动名词，约 1200 年有记录；paint 经古法语来自拉丁 pingere，其更早词根属重构。年代均为约数。

items.en: Reconstructed root *peig- meant 'to cut, mark by incision'; the step from 'decorate with cut marks' to 'decorate with colour' is presumed rather than attested.
items.cn: 重构词根 *peig- 意为「切、刻痕」；从「以刻痕装饰」到「以色彩装饰」的演变是推测，而非有直接书证。

items.en: Pingere meant 'to paint, represent in a picture, stain; embroider, tattoo'.
items.cn: pingere 意为「绘画、在图中表现、染色；刺绣、纹身」。

items.en: Old French peindre 'to paint' supplied the past participle peint, from which English paint derives.
items.cn: 古法语 peindre「绘画」提供过去分词 peint，英语 paint 由此而来。

items.en: English paint is recorded from the mid-thirteenth century, first for representing someone or something in paint.
items.cn: 英语 paint 自 13 世纪中叶有记录，最初指用颜料表现某人或某物。

items.en: Painting is recorded around 1200 for 'that which is painted, a picture'; by the late fourteenth century it also meant the art of depicting with paint.
items.cn: painting 约 1200 年有记录，指「被画成之物、图画」；到 14 世纪后期也指用颜料描绘的艺术。

items.en: From the general verb sense 'cover a surface with colour', the noun acquired the paintwork and trade senses.
items.cn: 从动词的一般义「用颜色覆盖表面」，名词获得了涂层与行业义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same paint- stock that differ in word class or result; group two holds words for pictures and surfaces made in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 paint- 词干、但词类或结果不同的词；第二组是用其他方式制作的图画与表面。

entries.definition: The person who paints; painting is the activity or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 作画或涂漆的人；painting 是活动或其产物。

entries.definition: To coat or depict, or the substance used; painting adds the result or activity suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 涂覆或描绘，或所用材料；painting 加上结果或活动后缀。

entries.definition: Describes a surface that has received paint; it is a participle, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已上漆的表面；是分词，而非名词。

entries.definition: Describes visible brushwork and a picture-like quality; it is a style judgement, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可见笔触与画面感；是风格判断，不是类别。

entries.definition: A picture made with lines, usually dry media; painting works with liquid colour and surface.
entries.definitionCN: 用线条、通常以干性媒材作的画；painting 使用液体颜料与表面。

entries.definition: Any visual representation, including photographs and prints; painting specifies the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 任何视觉再现，包括照片与版画；painting 限定媒介。

entries.definition: The woven surface for a painting, or a painting by metonymy; it names the support rather than the art.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画所用的织布表面，或以转喻指一幅画；命名的是支撑物而非艺术。

entries.definition: A layer of material covering a surface; it is the technical cousin of the paintwork sense.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖表面的材料层；是 painting 涂装义的技术近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paint + -ing: the activity or the thing made.
normal.cn: paint + -ing：活动，或做出来的东西。

normal.en: Latin pingere is the source, and the same stem gives picture and pigment.
normal.cn: 来源是拉丁 pingere，同一词干还给出 picture 与 pigment。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: oil painting, portrait painting, the painting of the bridge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：油画、肖像画、桥梁涂装。

normal.en: The family runs paint, painter, painting, painted, paintwork and painterly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 paint、painter、painting、painted、paintwork 与 painterly。

normal.en: A museum label says 'oil on canvas' but calls the object a painting.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签写「布面油画」，却把对象称作 painting。

abstract.en: Picture a wet stroke that cannot be undone without leaving a trace.
abstract.cn: 想象一道湿笔触，想撤掉总会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a flat surface becoming a window that is also an object.
abstract.cn: 想象一块平面变成既是窗又是物的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall and a canvas answering to the same action.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙与一块画布回应同一个动作。

examples.en: The painting was relined before the exhibition.
examples.cn: 这幅画在展览前做了托裱。

examples.en: Painting was taught alongside anatomy in the old academy.
examples.cn: 在旧式学院里，绘画与解剖学一起教授。

examples.en: The painting of the hall took longer than the carpentry.
examples.cn: 大厅的涂装比木工花的时间更长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paint（涂颜料）+ -ing」——涂出来的东西 → 画

root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画、染色」经古法语 peindre、过去分词 peint 进入英语 paint（13 世纪中叶）；painting 约 1200 年出现，兼指画作、绘画艺术与涂装。更早词根拟为 *peig-「刻痕」，属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the finished picture to the art form, the act, a school, a genre, a painted surface, the coating trade and a specific medium.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从完成的画作转到艺术门类、行为、画派、画类、涂层、涂装行业与具体媒介。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brush loaded with wet pigment crosses the cloth and leaves a mark that cannot return to nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支蘸满湿颜料的笔走过布面，留下一条无法回到空白的痕迹。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: the result, hanging on a wall.
branches.cn: 画作：结果，挂在墙上。

branches.en: ART AND MEDIUM: the whole discipline, then one technique inside it.
branches.cn: 艺术与媒介：整门学科，然后是其中一种技法。

branches.en: THE ACT: the doing, which the same suffix also names.
branches.cn: 行为：正在做的过程，同一后缀也能命名它。

branches.en: SCHOOL AND GENRE: shared habits across works, then a subject category.
branches.cn: 画派与画类：作品间的共同习惯，然后是题材类别。

branches.en: THE SURFACE TRADE: coating an object, then the industry that does it for hire.
branches.cn: 表面行业：给物件上涂层，然后是为报酬做这件事的行业。

intro.en: Painting is a verb stem plus the noun suffix -ing, and the stem builds a family of people, results and styles.
intro.cn: painting 是动词词干加名词后缀 -ing，同一词干还构成指人、结果与风格的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pingere is the ancestor; it also yields picture, pigment and depict, all through the idea of marking a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 祖先是拉丁 pingere；它还给出 picture、pigment 与 depict，都经由「在表面留下痕迹」这一观念。

items.structure: Old French peindre, from Latin pingere
items.meaning: to colour a surface; to depict
items.example: They painted the door blue.
items.exampleCN: 他们把门漆成蓝色。

items.example: Building and painting use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: building 与 painting 用同一个词尾。

items.meaning: a picture; the art or act
items.example: The painting hangs in the north room.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画挂在北厅。

items.example: The painter primed the wall.
items.exampleCN: 油漆工给墙上了底漆。

items.example: The painted shutters were new.
items.exampleCN: 上过漆的百叶窗是新的。

items.meaning: the painted surface of an object
items.example: The paintwork was chipped at the edge.
items.exampleCN: 边缘的漆面有剥落。

items.example: The photograph has a painterly softness.
items.exampleCN: 这张照片有一种绘画般的柔和。

items.meaning: to portray in an image or words
items.example: The seal depicts a lion.
items.exampleCN: 这枚印章描绘一头狮子。

items.example: The pigment faded in the light.
items.exampleCN: 颜料在光下褪色。

items.example: The picture shows the harbour.
items.exampleCN: 这幅图画显示港口。

definition_zh: n. 兴高采烈；得意洋洋；振奋
definition_en: a feeling of great joy and pride, usually after a success

intro.en: Elation is Latin elatio, a lifting up, from elatus, the participle of efferre, which joins ex- meaning out to ferre meaning to carry; the mood is carried upward.
intro.cn: elation 就是拉丁语 elatio（抬起），来自 elatus，它是 efferre 的分词，而 efferre 把 ex-（向外）与 ferre（携带）结合；情绪被向上抬了起来。

items.en: Latin ferre means to carry or bear.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 意为携带、承受。

items.en: Adding ex- gives efferre, to carry out or lift up.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 efferre，意为带出、抬起。

items.en: The participle elatus means lifted up, carried out.
items.cn: 分词 elatus 意为被抬起的、被带出的。

items.en: The noun elatio names a lifting up, later a lifting of the spirits.
items.cn: 名词 elatio 指抬起，后来指情绪高涨。

items.en: English took elation in the 14C for pride and high spirits.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 elation，指自豪与高昂情绪。

items.en: Psychology used elation for an elevated mood that can overshoot judgement.
items.cn: 心理学用 elation 指可能超出判断力的高涨情绪。

note.en: Elation and relation both end in -lation, from Latin latus, carried; elation is the mood carried up, relation is a thing carried back to another.
note.cn: elation 与 relation 都以 -lation 结尾，来自拉丁语 latus（被携带的）；elation 是被抬高的情绪，relation 是被带回另一事物的联系。

dict_mnemonic.text: elation ＝ e-（向外、向上，ex- 的变体）＋ lat（携带，拉丁 ferre／latus）＋ -ion（名词后缀）＝「被抬起来的状态」。情绪被抬高 → 兴高采烈、得意洋洋。同根换词尾：elate 动词「使兴奋」、elated 形容词「兴高采烈的」（人作主语：she was elated）、elatedly 副词、elating 形容词「令人兴奋的」（事作主语）。注意与 elation 押韵的 relation 也来自 latus（relatus 带回），但意思完全不同。近义梯度：elation 成功后的喜悦自豪；euphoria 强度更高的欣快（也用于医学）；exhilaration 带刺激感的振奋（运动、速度）；jubilation 公开表达的欢腾。反义方向是 dejection（de- 向下 ＋ ject 扔 ＝ 情绪被扔下去＝沮丧）。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、向上）＋ ferre（携带）→ efferre → elatus（被抬起的）→ elatio → elation（兴高采烈）

definition_zh: 灭绝；消亡；（权利、债务的）消灭；（星光）消光
definition_en: the dying out of a species or the ending of something altogether
core_image: 一排灯原本一盏接一盏亮着，最后一盏也熄掉，整排陷入黑暗
scene: 这里指「灭绝」。 The extinction of the passenger pigeon became a warning for conservationists.
sceneCN: 这里 extinction 指「一个物种彻底消失」（第 1 个义项：某物种的最后个体死亡，种群不再延续）；句意为旅鸽的灭绝成了自然保护者的警钟。图中可辨识物件：空荡的树枝、褪色的鸟形轮廓、标本柜、记录的日期。

pos.zh: 灭绝；消亡；消灭（可数，复数 extinctions）
