senses.title: A species dying out completely
senses.definition: the death of the last members of a species, so that it no longer exists
senses.definitionCN: 某物种最后个体死亡，从此不再存在
senses.example: The extinction of the passenger pigeon became a warning for conservationists.
senses.exampleCN: 旅鸽的灭绝成了自然保护者的警钟。
senses.why: extinction is the noun of extinguishing: a flame goes out and nothing of it is left, which is exactly the image used for a species.
senses.whyCN: extinction 是「熄灭」的名词：火苗灭掉后什么也不剩，物种灭绝用的正是这个意象。

senses.title: The process of dying out
senses.definition: the process by which the last members of a group decline and disappear
senses.definitionCN: 某类群最后的成员逐渐减少并消失的过程
senses.example: The extinction of the dodo unfolded over less than a century.
senses.exampleCN: 渡鸦的灭绝在不到一个世纪内展开。
senses.why: the noun names both the endpoint and the road to it, and the process reading is the one used in ecology.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既指终点也指通往终点的路，生态学用的是过程这一读法。

senses.title: Local extinction, or extirpation
senses.titleCN: 局部灭绝：某地消失但别处尚有
senses.definition: the disappearance of a species from one region while it survives elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 某物种在一个地区消失，但在别处仍然存在
senses.example: Wolves faced local extinction in the lowlands but held on in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 狼在低地遭遇局部灭绝，但在山区存续下来。
senses.why: because a species can vanish locally without vanishing globally, the noun takes a qualifier to mark the smaller scale.
senses.whyCN: 因为物种可以在本地消失而不在全球消失，这个名词需要限定语来标记较小的尺度。

senses.title: A mass extinction
senses.titleCN: 大灭绝：短时间内大量物种消失
senses.definition: an event in which a large share of all species disappears in a short span of geological time
senses.definitionCN: 在地质时间的短促跨度内，大比例物种消失的事件
senses.example: The end-Permian mass extinction removed most marine families.
senses.exampleCN: 二叠纪末大灭绝抹去了大多数海洋科。
senses.why: mass marks the scale, and extinction supplies the verb-derived idea of everything going out at once.
senses.whyCN: mass 标记规模，extinction 提供「一齐熄灭」的动词意象。

senses.title: A language or culture dying out
senses.definition: the disappearance of a language or way of life when its last speakers or practitioners die
senses.definitionCN: 语言或生活方式因最后使用者的离世而消失
senses.example: Linguists race to record languages facing extinction.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家争相记录面临消亡的语言。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the biological sense to anything whose carriers can die out, which is why languages are said to go extinct.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻把生物学含义移到任何「承载者会消亡」的事物上，因此语言也被说成灭绝。

senses.title: Dimming of starlight by dust
senses.titleCN: 天文学义：星际尘埃导致的星光消光
senses.definition: the absorption and scattering of starlight by interstellar matter
senses.definitionCN: 星际物质对星光的吸收与散射
senses.example: Interstellar dust causes the extinction of light from distant stars.
senses.exampleCN: 星际尘埃使远处恒星的光发生消光。
senses.why: astronomers borrowed the word because light is literally put out along the way, in the same sense as a flame.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家借用这个词，因为光确实在途中被「熄灭」，与火苗同理。

senses.title: A right or debt extinguished
senses.titleCN: 法律义：权利或债务的消灭
senses.definition: the ending of a legal right or obligation, as when a debt is paid off
senses.definitionCN: 某项法律权利或义务的终止，如债务清偿后消灭
senses.example: Payment produced the extinction of the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 付款使该债务归于消灭。
senses.why: law uses the word for anything that ceases to exist in the eyes of the law, keeping the core idea of being put out.
senses.whyCN: 法律用它指在法律眼中不复存在的事物，保留了「被熄灭」的核心。

senses.title: A conditioned response dying out
senses.titleCN: 行为心理学义：条件反应消退
senses.definition: the weakening and disappearance of a learned response when it is no longer reinforced
senses.definitionCN: 学习得来的反应因不再被强化而减弱并消失
senses.example: Extinction of the conditioned response followed repeated non-reinforcement.
senses.exampleCN: 在反复不予强化之后，条件反应出现了消退。
senses.why: psychology borrowed it for a response that fades away, treating the behaviour as the flame that goes out.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借它指逐渐消失的反应，把行为当作被熄灭的火。

intro.en: Extinction comes from Latin exstinctio, built on exstinguere 'to quench, put out', from ex- 'out' and stinguere 'to prick, quench'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: extinction 来自拉丁 exstinctio，基于 exstinguere「熄灭、扑灭」，由 ex-「向外」与 stinguere「刺、熄灭」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stinguere meant 'to prick or quench'. its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to a root meaning 'to stick, prick' is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated fact.
items.cn: stinguere 意为「刺、熄灭」。其更深来源不确定；把它连到表示「刺、扎」的词根只是重构，并非已证事实。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus stinguere gave exstinguere 'to put out, quench, destroy', used of fires, lights and, figuratively, of families.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 stinguere 得 exstinguere「扑灭、熄灭、毁掉」，用于火与光，也比喻家族断绝。

items.en: The noun exstinctio named a quenching or a putting out; English took it as extinction in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 exstinctio 指熄灭或扑灭；英语于 15 世纪以 extinction 吸收。

items.en: The sense of a species dying out is recorded from the nineteenth century, as naturalists assembled the fossil record of vanished forms.
items.cn: 物种灭绝的意思在 19 世纪有记录，当时博物学家整理已消失类型的化石记录。

items.en: The twentieth century added the astronomical sense of light extinction and the psychological sense of response extinction.
items.cn: 20 世纪又增添了天文学的「消光」义与心理学的「反应消退」义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and deeper root): the exact first citation of the biological sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of stinguere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：生物义的最早书证没有确定；stinguere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same stinguere stock that look alike; group two holds words for things ending, which differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 stinguere 词干、形似的词；第二组表示「终结」，范围不同。

entries.definition: The state of having died out; extinction is the event or process that produces that state.
entries.definitionCN: 指已灭绝的状态；extinction 是造成该状态的事件或过程。

entries.definition: To put out a fire or light, or to wipe out a right; the noun extinction is its result.
entries.definitionCN: 扑灭火或光，或使权利消灭；名词 extinction 是其结果。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus stinguere: to mark things apart, hence to tell them apart. It has nothing to do with dying out.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 stinguere：把事物区分开，因此指辨别。与灭绝无关。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus stinguere, literally 'pricked on': an inborn drive. The same root, a very different path.
entries.definitionCN: in-「在内」加 stinguere，字面为「被内在刺动」：天生的驱力。同根而走向完全不同。

entries.definition: The removal of a species from one area while it survives elsewhere; extinction means the species is gone everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物种在一地被清除而别处仍存；extinction 指该物种处处不见。

entries.definition: A sharp local loss of many individuals; it need not end the species.
entries.definitionCN: 指一地大量个体骤然死亡；未必导致物种终结。

entries.definition: A broad word for removing something, from rivals to waste; it lacks the biological finality of extinction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指去除，从对手到废物；不含 extinction 那种生物学上的终结性。

entries.definition: The fact of no longer being seen; a species may disappear from a survey and still return.
entries.definitionCN: 指不再被看见；物种可能从调查中消失却仍然回来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + stinguere 'quench': the flame is put right out.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」+ stinguere「熄灭」：火被彻底弄灭。

normal.en: The family runs extinction, extinct, extinguish, extinguisher, extinguishment.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 extinction、extinct、extinguish、extinguisher、extinguishment。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: mass extinction, extinction event, brink of extinction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模：大灭绝、灭绝事件、灭绝边缘。

normal.en: The same root shows in distinguish and instinct, both with different prefixes.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 distinguish 与 instinct 中，前缀都不同。

normal.en: Ecology counts local extinction separately from global extinction.
normal.cn: 生态学把局部灭绝与全球灭绝分开计数。

abstract.en: Picture the last candle in a row going out, and the room going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一排蜡烛的最后一支熄灭，房间陷入黑暗。

abstract.en: Picture a language with one elderly speaker left, and then none.
abstract.cn: 想象一门语言只剩一位老人会说，然后一个也不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a star whose light is eaten by dust before it reaches a telescope.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗星的光在到达望远镜前被尘埃吃掉。

examples.en: Habitat loss is the leading cause of extinction today.
examples.cn: 生境丧失是当今灭绝的首要原因。

examples.en: The extinction rate is now far above the fossil background.
examples.cn: 当前的灭绝速率远高于化石记录的背景值。

examples.en: The debt's extinction must be recorded in the ledger.
examples.cn: 债务的消灭必须记入账簿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ tinct（熄灭）」——火苗彻底熄掉，什么也不剩 → 灭绝、消亡

root: 拉丁 exstinctio「熄灭」来自 exstinguere（ex-「向外」+ stinguere「刺、熄灭」）；stinguere 更深来源不确定，与 distinguish、instinct 同根不同前缀。英语 extinction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: something is put out, and the putting-out is then read as a species, a process, a local loss, a mass event, a language, a beam of starlight, a legal right and a learned response.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个意象展开：某物被熄灭，这个「熄灭」再被读成物种、过程、局部丧失、大规模事件、语言、一束星光、法律权利与习得反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last flame of a row is put out and the row goes dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排火的最后一支被弄灭，整排陷入黑暗。

branches.en: SPECIES AND PROCESS: either the final state or the road that leads to it.
branches.cn: 物种与过程：或指终局状态，或指通向终局的路。

branches.en: SCALE MARKERS: a loss can be local, or vast enough to count as mass.
branches.cn: 尺度标记：丧失可以是局部的，也可以大到算作大灭绝。

branches.en: CARRIERS DIE OUT: languages and customs are treated as if they had last speakers.
branches.cn: 承载者消亡：语言与习俗被当作有「最后使用者」的事物。

branches.en: LIGHT PUT OUT: dust quenches starlight along the path.
branches.cn: 光被熄灭：尘埃在途中把星光弄灭。

branches.en: OTHER ENDINGS: rights and learned responses also cease to exist.
branches.cn: 其他终结：权利与习得反应同样不复存在。

intro.en: Extinction is a Latin noun of prefix plus root; ex- carries the sense of 'out', and the root also builds extinguish, distinguish and instinct.
intro.cn: extinction 是前缀加词根的拉丁名词；ex- 带「向外」的意思，同一词根还构成 extinguish、distinguish 与 instinct。

latinIntro.en: Latin exstinguere gives extinction, extinct and extinguish; dis- and in- versions of the same root give distinguish and instinct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 exstinguere 衍生 extinction、extinct 与 extinguish；同一词根的 dis- 与 in- 版本给出 distinguish 与 instinct。

items.example: The prefix marks the flame being driven out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标记火被赶出去。

items.example: The root supplies the quenching image.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「熄灭」的意象。

items.example: Mass extinction removed most marine families.
items.exampleCN: 大灭绝抹去了大多数海洋科。

items.example: The volcano is extinct.
items.exampleCN: 这座火山已经熄灭。

items.example: Crews extinguished the fire within an hour.
items.exampleCN: 消防队在小时内扑灭了火。

items.meaning: a device for putting out fires
items.example: The extinguisher sits by the door.
items.exampleCN: 灭火器放在门边。

items.meaning: to mark apart; to tell apart
items.example: The stripes distinguish the two species.
items.exampleCN: 条纹把这两个物种区分开。

items.example: The bird finds the route by instinct.
items.exampleCN: 这种鸟靠本能找到路线。

items.meaning: tending to put out or end
items.example: The extinctive clause ended the easement.
items.exampleCN: 那条消灭条款终止了地役权。

latinEntries.structure: exstinctus, exstincta, exstinctum (past participle used as adjective)

definition_zh: 实施；执行；进行；完成；履行；把……搬出去
definition_en: to perform or complete a plan, a task, an order or an action, or literally to move something out of a place
core_image: 工头把图纸摊在钢梁上，一名工人照着编号逐段加固，另一名在旁边把已完成的项一格一格打勾
scene: 旧厂房里，工人按图纸逐项施工，监理拿着清单在旁边核对每一项是否真的落实。 The crew will carry out the reinforcement exactly as the drawing shows.
sceneCN: 这里指按计划实施加固工程（第 1 个义项：把既定方案真正做出来）；句意为施工队将完全照图纸实施加固。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、图纸、打勾清单、扭矩扳手。

pos.zh: 实施；执行；进行（及物动词短语，宾语多为计划、研究、命令、任务）
把……搬出去（字面义，宾语为可移动的物件）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示施事者的词尾构成，义为「承运者；载体」
由动词加表示行为或工具的名词尾构成，义为「运输；车厢」
由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「搬运；承载的」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「便于携带的」

senses.title: Put a plan into effect
senses.definition: to perform a planned piece of work from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 把一项已规划的工作从头到尾做出来
senses.example: The city will carry out the drainage project in two stages.
senses.exampleCN: 该市将分两个阶段实施排水工程。
senses.why: The verb meant to move something along, and a plan is carried until it stands completed rather than only written.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「把某物搬运向前」，计划被「搬」到完工为止，而不是停在纸面上。

senses.title: Conduct a study
senses.definition: to perform a systematic inquiry or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 开展系统的调查或测量
senses.example: The team must carry out a survey of every household in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该团队必须对河谷中的每一户进行调查。
senses.why: A survey is carried outward into every household until the plan stands completed.
senses.whyCN: 调查被搬到每一户人家，直到计划完成。

senses.title: Fulfil a promise or an order
senses.definition: to act on a commitment or an instruction that has been given
senses.definitionCN: 把已作出的承诺或已下达的指示做出来
senses.example: Officers should carry out the order even when they doubt its wisdom.
senses.exampleCN: 即使对命令是否明智存疑，官员也应执行该命令。
senses.why: An order is only words until it is carried outward into action.
senses.whyCN: 命令在被搬进行动之前只是话。

senses.title: Complete a task to the end
senses.definition: to finish a piece of work rather than leave it partly done
senses.definitionCN: 把一件工作做完，而不是半途停下
senses.example: Volunteers can carry out the whole restoration in a single summer.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者可以在一个夏天内完成整个修复工作。
senses.why: The outward push ends only when the last piece is finished.
senses.whyCN: 向外的推力直到最后一件做完才停止。

senses.title: Mount a military action
senses.definition: to perform a raid, an attack or a patrol as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 以部队为单位实施突袭、攻击或巡逻
senses.example: The patrol may carry out a raid on the depot before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻队可能在黎明前对仓库实施突袭。
senses.why: A unit carries an action outward beyond its own lines.
senses.whyCN: 部队把行动搬到自己防线之外。

senses.title: Remove something physically
senses.definition: literally to take an object out of a room or a building
senses.definitionCN: 字面地把物件从房间或建筑中搬走
senses.example: Two workers will carry out the broken crates before the floor is washed.
senses.exampleCN: 两名工人会在洗地之前把破木箱搬出去。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the phrase: the object is carried and the direction is outward.
senses.whyCN: 这是短语最古老的一层：物件被搬动，方向朝外。

senses.title: Make a threat real
senses.definition: to actually do what one has warned others one would do
senses.definitionCN: 真的做出此前警告过要做的事
senses.example: He may carry out his threat to publish the letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他可能真的兑现公布那些信件的威胁。
senses.why: A threat becomes real only when it is carried out into the act it named.
senses.whyCN: 威胁只有在被搬成它所说的那个行动时才变真。

senses.title: Apply a reform at every level
senses.definition: to put a new rule into practice through every level of an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 使新规则在组织的每一层都落到实处
senses.example: Local offices must carry out the new rules without adding their own conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 地方办事处必须执行新规则，不得自行附加条件。
senses.why: A rule is carried outward through every office until the last one acts on it.
senses.whyCN: 规则被搬到每一个办事处，直到最后一个也照它行事。

senses.title: Execute a commercial transaction
senses.definition: to complete a sale or an order in a market
senses.definitionCN: 在市场里完成一笔买卖或订单
senses.example: The broker will carry out the sale at the opening price.
senses.exampleCN: 经纪人将按开盘价执行这笔卖出。
senses.why: A trade is carried to its close when the order is executed at the stated price.
senses.whyCN: 交易在按约定价格执行时被搬到终点。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a verb that reached English from the language of carters with a native particle of direction. What is carried out is moved from inside to outside, and the figurative senses keep that outward push.
intro.cn: 这个短语把经赶车人之语进入英语的动词，与本族表示方向的虚词配在一起。被「搬出去」的东西由内到外，比喻义也保留这股向外的推力。

items.en: A Gaulish word for a wheeled cart was taken into Latin as carrus, and it stands behind carriage, cargo and career.
items.cn: 高卢语中表示带轮车子的词被拉丁语吸收，马车、货物与「生涯」诸词都由它而来。

items.en: Carricare meant to load a cart, and it produced the verb that French reshaped as carier, to carry.
items.cn: 这个词意为「把货装上车」，由此产生的动词被法语改写成「运送」。

items.en: English took the verb through the northern French form in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经北方法语的形式引入这个动词。

items.en: The particle is native English and means outward or away from the inside; it gives the phrase its direction.
items.cn: 虚词是本族英语，意为「向外、离开里面」，为短语提供了方向。

items.en: The combination first appears in the sixteenth century with the literal sense, and the sense of performing a plan follows. The exact first citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of the cart word is not established.
items.cn: 这个组合在十六世纪先以字面义出现，随后才有「实施计划」的意思。最早书证年代不确定；表示「车」的那个词更早的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the carrying verb with a different particle each time; the second group holds verbs of performing a task.
note.cn: 第一组共享「搬运」动词，但各自的虚词不同；第二组是表示「执行任务」的动词。

entries.definition: The bare verb needs a concrete object and no direction, as carry a bag; it says nothing about completing a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时带具体宾语，如提一个包，不含方向，也不表示完成计划。

entries.definition: It means to continue rather than to perform; the particle points forward in time, not outward.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「继续」，而不是「执行」；虚词指时间上的向前，而非向外。

entries.definition: It means to complete something despite difficulty, close to the fourth sense but with an added note of endurance.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「排除困难坚持完成」，接近第四个义项，但多了一层「撑住」的意味。

entries.definition: It means to transfer something to another period or account, a movement across, not an execution.
entries.definitionCN: 意为把某物结转到另一期或另一账目，是横向转移，不是执行。

entries.definition: A formal verb for making a policy or system operate; it stresses the machinery of putting something into effect.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地表示使政策或制度运转，强调「使之生效」的机制。

entries.definition: The usual verb for running a study, a survey or an orchestra; it fits research better than repairs.
entries.definitionCN: 常用于「进行研究、调查或指挥乐队」，用于研究比用于维修更合适。

entries.definition: A formal verb for performing a plan or a legal act; it also carries the separate meaning of putting someone to death.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地表示执行计划或法律行为；另有「处死」这一不相干的含义。

entries.definition: A general verb for doing a task or a role; it lacks the sense of completing something previously planned.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指完成任务或扮演角色，不含「把既定计划做完」之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the reinforcement drawing, the household survey, the order on the desk and the crates by the door.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用加固图纸、入户调查、桌上的命令与门边的木箱四个场景。

normal.en: A drawing on a steel beam, a torque wrench, and a checklist filling with ticks.
normal.cn: 钢梁上摊着图纸，扭矩扳手转动，清单上的勾一格一格填满。

normal.en: One survey sheet for every household in the valley.
normal.cn: 河谷里每户一张调查表。

normal.en: An order signed at the top, carried out before the ink is dry.
normal.cn: 命令签在顶端，墨迹未干就已经执行。

normal.en: Broken crates carried out before the floor is washed.
normal.cn: 洗地之前，先把破木箱搬出去。

normal.en: A threat that stops being words and becomes an act.
normal.cn: 威胁不再只是话，而变成了一件事。

abstract.en: A plan is only a sentence until someone carries it out.
abstract.cn: 计划在有人执行之前，只是一句话。

abstract.en: The same phrase moves a box and a reform, because both travel from intention to fact.
abstract.cn: 同一个短语既搬箱子也推改革，因为两者都从意图走到事实。

abstract.en: Execution is where authority meets material: nothing survives the trip unchanged.
abstract.cn: 执行是权威与材料相遇的地方：经过这趟搬运，没有东西原样不变。

examples.en: The laboratory will carry out the tests under a sealed protocol.
examples.cn: 实验室将按封存的规程进行这些测试。

examples.en: Local councils must carry out the housing survey before winter.
examples.cn: 地方议会必须在入冬前完成住房调查。

examples.en: A promise is easy to make and harder to carry out.
examples.cn: 承诺容易作出，却难以履行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「凯瑞 奥特」：把「搬出去」记成工人把箱子从屋里抬到门外——搬到底，事情就算做完

root: 核心动词经古法语来自晚期拉丁语「把货物装上车」，其源头是高卢语中表示「车」的词，更早来源不确定；虚词为本族英语，意为「向外」。短语整体表示「把某事从计划搬到完成」，也保留字面的「搬出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move outward: a plan, a study, an order, a task, a raid, a crate, a threat, a reform at every level, and a sale.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都朝外推：计划、研究、命令、任务、突袭、木箱、威胁、层层落实的改革与一笔交易。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawing laid on a steel beam, a wrench turning, and a checklist filling with ticks as the work moves outward to completion.
core.cn: 核心意象：图纸摊在钢梁上，扳手转动，清单随工程推进被一格格打勾，直到完成。

branches.en: THE PLAN AND THE LEVELS: a project or a rule must be performed from the top down to the last office.
branches.cn: 计划与层级：工程或规则必须从上到下落到最后一个办事处。

branches.en: THE FIELD ACTION: a survey in every household, a raid before dawn.
branches.cn: 现场行动：逐户调查，黎明突袭。

branches.en: THE BINDING WORD: an order obeyed, a threat finally acted on.
branches.cn: 有约束的话：命令被服从，威胁终于变成行动。

branches.en: THE CLOSED DEAL: the restoration finished, the sale executed at the opening price.
branches.cn: 完成的交易：修复完工，卖出按开盘价执行。

branches.en: THE LITERAL BOX: crates taken out before the floor is washed.
branches.cn: 字面的箱子：洗地之前把木箱搬出去。

intro.en: The family joins a borrowed cart word to native English endings; the particle carries direction while the endings carry agent, act and capacity.
intro.cn: 这个词族把借来的「车」之词与本族英语词尾结合；方向由虚词承担，施事、动作与能力由词尾承担。

latinIntro.en: Latin carrus came from Gaulish, and its verb carricare passed through French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「车」来自高卢语，其动词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The borrowed noun at the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 词族底层的借入名词。

items.example: It produced the verb of carrying.
items.exampleCN: 它产生了「运送」的动词。

items.example: The form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入的那个形式。

items.example: The English verb at the centre of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 短语中心的英语动词。

items.example: It forms the word for a carrier.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「承运者」的词。

items.example: It forms the noun for transport and its price.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示运输及其费用的名词。

items.example: It supplies the outward direction.
items.exampleCN: 它提供向外的方向。

items.example: It forms the participle of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它构成短语的现在分词。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施事词尾构成，义为「承运者」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「运输；车厢」
由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「搬运；承载的」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「便于携带的」

definition_zh: 蛋白质；由氨基酸链折叠成特定形状的生物大分子；膳食中提供氨基酸的营养成分
definition_en: a large molecule built from a chain of amino acids and folded into a working shape, and by extension the nutrient class that supplies such molecules
core_image: 一串彩色珠子被揉成一团，表面有凹槽与凸起，正好能卡住另一块形状互补的珠子团
scene: 营养师说每餐都要有足够的蛋白质。 A protein folds into a shape that lets it bind one substrate and one partner, and nothing else.
sceneCN: 这里 protein 指「蛋白质分子」（第 1 个义项：由氨基酸链折叠成的生物大分子）；形状决定了它能结合谁。图中可辨识物件：珠链、折叠成的团块、表面凹槽、互补的结合面；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 蛋白质（可数，复数 proteins；指该物质整体时也可不可数）

derivatives.zh: 蛋白质组
蛋白质组学
蛋白酶
蛋白质的；蛋白状的
蛋白质水解

senses.title: A chain folded into a working shape
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质：折叠成形的氨基酸链
senses.definition: a macromolecule made of one or more chains of amino acids folded into a defined three-dimensional shape
senses.definitionCN: 由一条或多条氨基酸链折叠成确定三维形状的生物大分子
senses.example: Haemoglobin is a protein built from four folded chains.
senses.exampleCN: 血红蛋白是由四条折叠链构成的蛋白质。
senses.why: Greek prōteios meant 'primary', and the name was given because such substances were thought to be the primary stuff of nutrition; the modern molecule sense grew from that label.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 prōteios 意为「首要的」，命名时认为这类物质是营养的首要成分；现代「分子」义正是在这个标签上发展出来的。

senses.title: Sequence and fold
senses.definition: the internal plan of a protein: the order of amino acids and the way that order folds
senses.definitionCN: 蛋白质的内部方案：氨基酸的排列顺序，以及这一顺序折叠的方式
senses.example: A single wrong amino acid can spoil the fold of the whole protein.
senses.exampleCN: 一个氨基酸出错就可能毁掉整个蛋白质的折叠。
senses.why: once the chain was sequenced, the word covered not only the substance but the architecture that makes it work.
senses.whyCN: 当链被测序后，这个词不仅指物质，也指让它工作的构造。

senses.title: The nutrient on a plate
senses.titleCN: 营养义：膳食中的蛋白质
senses.definition: the component of food that supplies amino acids, spoken of in amounts and quality
senses.definitionCN: 食物中提供氨基酸的成分，常按数量与质量来谈
senses.example: Beans and rice together supply a complete set of protein.
senses.exampleCN: 豆类与米饭搭配可提供完整的蛋白质。
senses.why: because the molecule is what the body rebuilds from food, the same word names the nutrient class on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 因为身体正是用食物重建这种分子，同一个词也指盘中的那类营养素。

senses.title: A job description, not a shape
senses.titleCN: 功能类别：按工作分工的蛋白质
senses.definition: a class of molecules grouped by what they do, such as enzymes, structural proteins, transporters and signals
senses.definitionCN: 按功能归类的分子，如酶、结构蛋白、运输蛋白与信号蛋白
senses.example: Collagen is a structural protein; insulin is a signal protein.
senses.exampleCN: 胶原蛋白是结构蛋白；胰岛素是信号蛋白。
senses.why: since shape serves a task, the word is also used to sort proteins by the task rather than by the fold.
senses.whyCN: 由于形状服务于任务，这个词也被用来按任务而非按折叠方式给蛋白质分类。

senses.title: Measured in a lab
senses.titleCN: 表达与水平：实验中的蛋白量
senses.definition: the amount of a particular protein made by a cell or sample, as measured in experiments
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或样本中某种特定蛋白质的生成量，以实验方式测定
senses.example: The tumour showed high protein expression of the receptor.
senses.exampleCN: 该肿瘤中受体的蛋白表达量很高。
senses.why: laboratory practice turns the substance into a quantity, so 'protein' can mean a measured level rather than a molecule.
senses.whyCN: 实验室实践把这种物质变成一种量，因此 protein 可以指被测定的水平，而非分子本身。

senses.title: Separated and detected
senses.titleCN: 纯化与检测：实验台上的蛋白操作
senses.definition: the substance as an object of purification, blotting and detection
senses.definitionCN: 作为纯化、印迹与检测对象的该物质
senses.example: The protein was purified from bacterial cultures and run on a gel.
senses.exampleCN: 该蛋白从细菌培养物中纯化，并在凝胶上电泳。
senses.why: methods name their object by the material, so a gel band or a blot is simply called protein.
senses.whyCN: 方法学以其材料来命名对象，因此凝胶条带或印迹就被直接称为 protein。

senses.title: The whole set at once
senses.definition: the entire complement of proteins in a cell or tissue, studied as a set
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或组织中全部蛋白质的总体，作为一个集合来研究
senses.example: Proteomic analysis compares thousands of proteins between healthy and sick tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质组分析比较健康与患病组织间数千种蛋白质。
senses.why: high-throughput methods made the collective countable, so the singular word can also stand for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 高通量方法使这个集合变得可计数，因此单数形式也可指整个集合。

senses.title: Designed and rebuilt
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质工程：改造与设计
senses.definition: a molecule treated as something that can be redesigned, fused or synthesized
senses.definitionCN: 被当作可以重新设计、融合或合成的分子的蛋白质
senses.example: Engineers added a tag to the protein so it could be captured.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师给该蛋白加了一个标签，以便把它捕获。
senses.why: when folding is understood as a code, the substance becomes a design space, and the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 当折叠被理解为一种编码，这种物质就成了设计空间，这个词也随之进入该用法。

intro.en: Protein was coined in 1838 from Greek prōteios 'primary', a word built on prōtos 'first'. It reached English through French protéine.
intro.cn: protein 于 1838 年由希腊 prōteios「首要的」造出，该词基于 prōtos「第一」。它经法语 protéine 进入英语。

items.en: prōtos meant 'first, foremost', and prōteios 'primary, of the first rank'. The compound behind them is a Greek formation, not a Latin one.
items.cn: prōtos 意为「第一、最前」，prōteios 意为「首要的、第一等的」。其背后的构词属希腊语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: Jöns Jacob Berzelius proposed the name protéine for the substance Mulder described as a primary constituent of living matter. The date is well recorded; the exact wording of the proposal is not.
items.cn: Jöns Jacob Berzelius 为 Mulder 所述「生命物质的首要成分」提议了 protéine 这一名称。年份有明确记录，提议的原话则无存。

items.en: Generally thought: the name reflects the belief that this substance was the primary material of nutrition and of the body; the reasoning is reported second-hand and not fully documented.
items.cn: 一般认为，这个名字反映了当时认为该物质是营养与身体的首要材料；其推理为二手记载，并未完整留存。

items.en: English protein appears in the nineteenth century through French; the earliest citation is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 protein 于 19 世纪经法语传入；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Twentieth-century chemistry established the amino acid chain and the folded structure, widening the word from a substance to an architecture.
items.cn: 20 世纪的化学确立了氨基酸链与折叠结构，把该词从一种物质扩展到一种构造。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of prōtos before Greek is unsettled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction; the earliest English date for protein is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：prōtos 在希腊语之前的来源并无定论，凡给出的印欧形式均属重构；protein 的最早英语书证亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that are often mistaken for relatives; group two holds words that name related molecules or roles.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误认为同族的形近词；第二组是命名相关分子或角色的词。

entries.tag: not from pr tos at all
entries.definition: Means 'ever-changing, versatile', from Proteus, the shape-shifting sea god. It shares letters with protein but comes from a different Greek name.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「多变、多才多艺」，来自会变形的海神 Proteus；与 protein 只是拼写相近，来源是另一个希腊专名。

entries.definition: A protein-digesting enzyme. It is named with -ase 'enzyme', so it is a tool that acts on proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指分解蛋白质的酶；由 -ase「酶」构成，是作用于蛋白质的工具。

entries.definition: All the proteins of a cell or tissue, named with -ome 'complete set'. It is a collection, not one molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个细胞或组织的全部蛋白质，由 -ome「全集」构成；是集合，不是单个分子。

entries.definition: A short amino acid chain, from Greek peptos 'digested', not from prōtos. Peptides are shorter than proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指短氨基酸链，来自希腊 peptos「被消化的」，并非 prōtos；肽比蛋白质短。

entries.definition: A long chain of amino acids before folding is considered; a protein is the folded, working object.
entries.definitionCN: 指尚未考虑折叠的长氨基酸链；protein 指折叠后能工作的对象。

entries.definition: A catalyst made of protein or RNA. Many enzymes are proteins, but not all proteins are enzymes.
entries.definitionCN: 由蛋白质或 RNA 构成的催化剂；许多酶是蛋白质，但并非所有蛋白质都是酶。

entries.definition: The single building block; a protein is a chain of them.
entries.definitionCN: 单个构建单元；蛋白质是由它们连成的链。

entries.definition: Any substance that nourishes. Protein is one nutrient among several, alongside fat and carbohydrate.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何提供营养的物质；蛋白质是与脂肪、碳水化合物并列的一种营养素。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prōteios 'primary': the substance once thought to be the first stuff of the body.
normal.cn: prōteios「首要的」：这曾被当作身体的第一种材料。

normal.en: The family runs protein, proteome, proteomics, proteinase, proteolysis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 protein、proteome、proteomics、proteinase、proteolysis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: protein structure, protein folding, protein expression, protein purification.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：蛋白质结构、折叠、表达、纯化。

normal.en: A protein is a chain that folds; a peptide is a short chain; an enzyme is one kind of protein.
normal.cn: 蛋白质是折叠的链；肽是短链；酶是蛋白质的一种。

normal.en: Structure decides function: the fold makes the pocket, and the pocket decides the partner.
normal.cn: 结构决定功能：折叠造出凹槽，凹槽决定结合对象。

abstract.en: Picture a necklace of coloured beads crushed into a ball with dents and ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象一条彩色珠链被揉成一团，表面有凹坑与凸棱。

abstract.en: Picture a key that is also made of beads, so its shape can be rewritten bead by bead.
abstract.cn: 想象一把也由珠子构成的钥匙，其形状可以逐颗改写。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen where the same ingredient is used as fuel, as brick and as signal.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，同一种材料既当燃料，又当砖块，还当信号。

examples.en: Heating denatures the protein, so the egg white turns solid.
examples.cn: 加热使蛋白质变性，因此蛋白凝固。

examples.en: Athletes often eat more protein than they strictly need.
examples.cn: 运动员常摄入超过实际所需的蛋白质。

examples.en: The protein was tagged with a fluorescent label for imaging.
examples.cn: 该蛋白被加上荧光标签以便成像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）上去的（tein）一团」——氨基酸连成链再揉成一团，构成身体的首要材料 → 蛋白质

root: 希腊 prōtos「第一」→ prōteios「首要的」→ 法语 protéine（1838，Berzelius 提议）→ 英语 protein。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a chain folds into a shape, and that shape is then read as an architecture, a nutrient, a job class, a measured level, a laboratory object, a whole set, and finally a design space.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一条链折叠成一个形状，而这个形状依次被读成构造、营养素、岗位类别、测定值、实验对象、全集，最后是设计空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bead chain crumpled into a lump whose dents fit one partner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条珠链被揉成团块，其凹处只与一个对象相合。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: the folded chain is the basic referent of the word.
branches.cn: 分子本身：折叠的链是该词的基本所指。

branches.en: ARCHITECTURE: sequence plus fold, the plan behind the shape.
branches.cn: 构造：序列加折叠，即形状背后的方案。

branches.en: NUTRIENT: the same substance read as food on a plate.
branches.cn: 营养素：同一种物质被读成盘中的食物。

branches.en: JOB CLASS: proteins sorted by task rather than by fold.
branches.cn: 岗位类别：按任务而非按折叠方式分类的蛋白质。

branches.en: QUANTITY AND DESIGN: measured levels, bench objects, whole sets, and molecules rewritten by engineers.
branches.cn: 数量与设计：测定水平、实验台对象、全集，以及被工程师改写的分子。

intro.en: Protein is a Greek-derived noun carrying a Greek suffix -eios; English adds the usual Latin-based endings for its family.
intro.cn: protein 是带希腊后缀 -eios 的希腊派生名词；英语为其词族加上通常的拉丁式词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no classical Latin source. New Latin proteinum is a Latinized spelling, while -ase, -ome and proteo- are modern scientific combining forms.
latinIntro.cn: 没有古典拉丁来源。新拉丁语 proteinum 是拉丁化拼写，而 -ase、-ome 与 proteo- 是现代科学组合形式。

items.meaning: the primary substance of nutrition; a folded amino acid chain
items.meaningCN: 营养的首要物质；折叠的氨基酸链
items.example: The protein binds calcium at its centre.
items.exampleCN: 该蛋白在中心结合钙。

items.example: Membrane proteins transport ions across the bilayer.
items.exampleCN: 膜蛋白把离子运过脂双层。

items.meaningCN: 由蛋白质构成的；蛋白状的
items.example: A proteinaceous coat surrounds the spore.
items.exampleCN: 一层蛋白性质的外壳包裹着孢子。

items.example: A serine proteinase digests the collagen.
items.exampleCN: 一种丝氨酸蛋白酶消化胶原。

items.example: Proteolysis releases the active hormone.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质水解会释放出活性激素。

items.meaning: all proteins of a cell or tissue
items.meaningCN: 细胞或组织的全部蛋白质
items.example: The proteome changes with stress.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质组会随压力改变。

items.meaningCN: 大规模研究蛋白质的学科
items.example: Proteomics needs sensitive mass spectrometers.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质组学需要灵敏的质谱仪。

items.example: Only proteogenic amino acids enter the chain.
items.exampleCN: 只有生蛋白氨基酸能进入链中。

items.example: Protease removes the signal peptide.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白酶切去信号肽。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 蛋白质（拉丁化科学名称）

definition_zh: 线粒体的；与线粒体有关的；由线粒体编码、介导或定位的
definition_en: relating to a mitochondrion, or produced, encoded, controlled or located within mitochondria
core_image: 一个细胞器被虚线框住，框线上贴着写有「属于它」的标签，框内的部件都染上同一种颜色
scene: 这里指「线粒体的」。 Mitochondrial DNA passes from mother to child, so it traces a single maternal line.
sceneCN: 这里 mitochondrial 指「线粒体自有的（由线粒体基因组编码的）」（第 3 个义项：由线粒体 DNA 编码或存在于其中的）；因此线粒体 DNA 只沿母系传递。图中可辨识物件：虚线框、标签、环状 DNA、母系箭头。

pos.zh: 线粒体的；与线粒体相关的（通常不作定语以外的名词用）

derivatives.zh: 线粒体（单数）
线粒体（复数）
在线粒体层面地
线粒体病
线粒体生成

senses.title: Belonging to the organelle
senses.definition: relating to or belonging to a mitochondrion
senses.definitionCN: 属于线粒体或与线粒体有关的
senses.example: Mitochondrial proteins are made partly in the cytosol and partly inside the organelle.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体蛋白一部分在细胞质中制造，一部分在细胞器内制造。
senses.why: the suffix -al turns the organelle's name into a label of belonging, so the adjective begins as a simple possessive.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把细胞器的名称变成表示归属的标签，因此这个形容词的起点只是一个简单的所属关系。

senses.title: Located inside the organelle
senses.definition: situated or occurring inside mitochondria
senses.definitionCN: 位于线粒体内部或在线粒体内发生的
senses.example: Mitochondrial calcium uptake shapes the organelle's response to stress.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体对钙的摄取塑造了该细胞器对压力的反应。
senses.why: once a thing has a boundary, the adjective can also mark where an event happens, not only whom it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物有了边界，这个形容词也能标记事件发生的位置，而不只是所属关系。

senses.title: Encoded by the organelle's own genome
senses.titleCN: 线粒体编码的：自身基因组来源
senses.definition: encoded by the small genome carried inside mitochondria rather than by the nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 由线粒体内部携带的小基因组编码，而不是由细胞核编码
senses.example: Only thirteen proteins in humans are fully mitochondrial.
senses.exampleCN: 人类只有十三种蛋白质完全由线粒体基因编码。
senses.why: the organelle turned out to hold its own instructions, so 'mitochondrial' came to mark origin of code as well as place.
senses.whyCN: 该细胞器被发现自带指令，于是 mitochondrial 除了地点，也开始标记「编码来源」。

senses.title: Inherited through the mother
senses.titleCN: 母系遗传的：沿卵细胞传递
senses.definition: passed down through the maternal line because mitochondria travel in the egg, not the sperm
senses.definitionCN: 因线粒体随卵细胞而非精子传递，故沿母系向下遗传
senses.example: Mitochondrial inheritance explains why affected mothers pass the trait to all children.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体遗传解释了为何受累母亲会把该性状传给所有子女。
senses.why: because the genome sits outside the nucleus, its inheritance rule is separate, and the adjective names that route.
senses.whyCN: 因为这份基因组在核外，其遗传规则自成一套，这个形容词命名的正是那条路径。

senses.title: Of disease caused by organelle failure
senses.titleCN: 线粒体病的：由细胞器功能障碍引起
senses.definition: describing disease that arises from faulty mitochondrial function or genome
senses.definitionCN: 描述由线粒体功能或基因组缺陷引发的疾病
senses.example: Patients with mitochondrial disease often show muscle weakness first.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体病患者常先出现肌无力。
senses.why: when the power plant fails, the whole body suffers, so the adjective attaches to a clinical category.
senses.whyCN: 当发电厂出故障，全身都会受损，于是这个形容词附着在一个临床类别上。

senses.title: Of the membranes and their potential
senses.titleCN: 线粒体膜的：膜与膜电位
senses.definition: relating to the organelle's membranes, especially the inner membrane and its electrical potential
senses.definitionCN: 与线粒体膜相关，尤其指内膜及其电位
senses.example: A fall in mitochondrial membrane potential is an early sign of damage.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体膜电位下降是损伤的早期信号。
senses.why: the adjective narrows from the whole organelle to its two skins, because that is where the electrical work happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从整个细胞器收窄到它的两层皮，因为电学工作正发生在那里。

senses.title: Targeted to the organelle
senses.titleCN: 靶向线粒体的：研究与药物用语
senses.definition: describing a probe, drug or signal that is deliberately directed to mitochondria
senses.definitionCN: 描述被有意导向线粒体的探针、药物或信号
senses.example: The team designed a mitochondrial antioxidant to reach the matrix.
senses.exampleCN: 团队设计了一种线粒体抗氧化剂以进入基质。
senses.why: research practice adds a purposive sense: the adjective now marks a destination chosen by a designer.
senses.whyCN: 科研实践加入了一层目的义：这个形容词现在标记一个由设计者选定的目的地。

senses.title: The cell's energetic core, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 引申义：细胞能量核心的
senses.definition: used figuratively for whatever supplies the driving energy of a system
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何为系统提供驱动能量的事物
senses.example: The city's mitochondrial role is played by its port.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市里扮演「线粒体」角色的是它的港口。
senses.why: as the organelle stands for energy supply itself, the adjective can be borrowed for any source of power.
senses.whyCN: 当这个细胞器本身就是能量供应的代名词，这个形容词便可借指任何动力来源。

intro.en: Mitochondrial is the English adjective on mitochondrion, with the Latin suffix -alis; the base is a Greek compound coined in 1898.
intro.cn: mitochondrial 是以 mitochondrion 为词干、加拉丁后缀 -alis 构成的英语形容词；词干是 1898 年创造的希腊合成词。

items.en: mitos 'thread' plus chondrion 'small granule' produced mitochondrium; the adjective inherits that compound unchanged.
items.cn: mitos「线」加 chondrion「小颗粒」产生 mitochondrium；形容词原样继承这个合成词。

items.en: Latin -alis formed adjectives of relation, as in naturalis from natura. English keeps it as -al, so mitochondrion gives mitochondrial.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 构成表示关系的形容词，如 natura 变 naturalis。英语保留为 -al，于是 mitochondrion 变 mitochondrial。

items.en: New Latin mitochondrium is a Latinized spelling, not an inherited word; no classical Latin root can be claimed for the base.
items.cn: 新拉丁语 mitochondrium 是拉丁化拼写，不是传承词；不应为该词干主张古典拉丁词根。

items.en: The adjective appears in English cytology in the early twentieth century, soon after the noun; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 该形容词于 20 世纪初随名词进入英语细胞学文献；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Work on mitochondrial genetics in the mid-twentieth century fixed the senses 'encoded by' and 'inherited through the mother'.
items.cn: 20 世纪中期的线粒体遗传学研究固定了「由……编码」与「经母系遗传」两个义项。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of the adjective is not recorded, and its derivational order relative to the noun is also unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词的最早英语书证无确切记录；其与名词的派生先后亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the same stem but differ in part of speech or in the organelle named; group two holds adjectives that answer a similar question about location or cause.
note.cn: 第一组是共享词干、但词性或所指细胞器不同的词；第二组是回答相同位置或来源问题的形容词。

entries.definition: The organelle itself, a count noun. Use it where a thing is meant, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞器本身，是可数名词；需要指事物而非性质时用它。

entries.definition: Cell division named from thread-like chromosomes; same Greek piece, entirely different process.
entries.definitionCN: 因染色体呈线状而得名的一种细胞分裂；希腊构件相同，所指过程完全不同。

entries.definition: A cartilage cell. Sharing chondros 'cartilage' does not make it an organelle word.
entries.definitionCN: 软骨细胞；虽共享 chondros「软骨」，仍与细胞器无关。

entries.definition: Means 'at the level of mitochondria' and modifies a verb or adjective; it cannot modify a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「在线粒体层面」，修饰动词或形容词，不能修饰名词。

entries.definition: Located in the cytoplasm, that is, outside the organelle; it is the contrasted location, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 位于细胞质，即细胞器之外；它是相对立的位置，而非同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to organelles in general. Mitochondrial specifies which organelle, so the two differ in precision.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与细胞器相关；mitochondrial 指明是哪一个细胞器，二者精确度不同。

entries.definition: Inside a cell but not tied to any one compartment; it is a wider location word.
entries.definitionCN: 在细胞内，但不限于某一区室；是范围更宽的位置词。

entries.definition: Describes a process that needs oxygen. Mitochondrial respiration is aerobic, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 描述需要氧的过程；线粒体呼吸是有氧的，但两词回答的不是同一个问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mitochondrion + -al: the '-al' is the same relational suffix as in natural and structural.
normal.cn: mitochondrion + -al：这个 -al 与 natural、structural 中的关系后缀相同。

normal.en: The family runs mitochondrion, mitochondria, mitochondrial, mitochondrially, mitochondriopathy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mitochondrion、mitochondria、mitochondrial、mitochondrially、mitochondriopathy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mitochondrial DNA, membrane potential, dysfunction, biogenesis, inheritance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：线粒体 DNA、膜电位、功能障碍、生成、遗传。

normal.en: Clinical use is easy to recall because the organelle's failure weakens muscle first.
normal.cn: 临床用法好记，因为该细胞器出故障时最先受累的是肌肉。

normal.en: The -al adjective answers 'whose?', 'where?' or 'made by whom?', and the context picks one.
normal.cn: 这个 -al 形容词回答「谁的」「在哪」「由谁制造」，由上下文选定其中之一。

abstract.en: Picture a dashed box drawn around one organelle, with everything inside tinted the same colour.
abstract.cn: 想象给一个细胞器画上虚线框，框内一切染成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a factory with its own small rulebook, separate from the city's law book.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂自带一本小规则书，与城市的法典分开。

abstract.en: Picture a power source so central that other buildings are named after the energy they draw from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个动力源如此核心，以至于其他建筑都以它们从中获取的能量来命名。

examples.en: Mitochondrial proteins must cross two membranes to reach the matrix.
examples.cn: 线粒体蛋白要穿过两层膜才能到达基质。

examples.en: Exercise increases mitochondrial biogenesis in trained muscle.
examples.cn: 运动会使受训肌肉的线粒体生成增加。

examples.en: The drug was designed to spare mitochondrial function.
examples.cn: 该药被设计为不损害线粒体功能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「线粒体（mitochondrion）加个 -al」——凡贴上线粒体标签的 → 线粒体的、线粒体内的

root: 希腊 mitos「线」+ chondrion「小颗粒」→ 新拉丁 mitochondrium（1898）→ 英语名词 mitochondrion + 拉丁关系后缀 -alis → mitochondrial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one possessive suffix: a thing belongs to the organelle, then lies inside it, is coded by it, is inherited through it, is diseased through it, is specified to its membranes, is aimed at it, or finally stands for energy itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个表所属的后缀散开：先属于该细胞器，再位于其内、由其编码、经其遗传、因其而病、具体到其膜、被有意指向它，最后甚至代指能量本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dashed boundary drawn around one organelle, tinting everything inside as 'its'.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一个细胞器画出的虚线边界，把其中一切都染成「它的」。

branches.en: POSSESSION: the plainest reading, a label of belonging attached by -al.
branches.cn: 所属：最朴素的读法，即由 -al 附上的归属标签。

branches.en: LOCATION: the boundary also marks where an event takes place.
branches.cn: 位置：边界同时标记事件发生的地点。

branches.en: ORIGIN OF CODE AND ROUTE: the organelle's own genome and the maternal path it travels.
branches.cn: 编码来源与传递路径：细胞器自有基因组，以及它沿母系传递的路径。

branches.en: FAILURE: when this boundary malfunctions, the adjective names a clinical category.
branches.cn: 故障：当这条边界失灵，该形容词命名一个临床类别。

branches.en: NARROWING AND EXTENDING: from the two membranes, to a chosen target, to any source of power.
branches.cn: 收窄与外扩：从两层膜，到被选定的靶点，再到任何动力来源。

intro.en: The adjective is a Greek scientific stem plus the Latin relational suffix -alis; the suffix does the grammatical work.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊科学词干加拉丁关系后缀 -alis 构成；语法工作由后缀承担。

latinIntro.en: No inherited Latin base exists; only the suffix -alis is Latin, and New Latin mitochondrium is a re-spelling of the Greek compound.
latinIntro.cn: 没有传承的拉丁词干；只有后缀 -alis 属拉丁语，新拉丁语 mitochondrium 只是希腊合成词的改写。

items.example: Mitochondrial membranes are rich in cardiolipin.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体膜富含心磷脂。

items.example: The pathway is mitochondrially regulated.
items.exampleCN: 该通路受线粒体调控。

items.example: Each mitochondrion has its own genome.
items.exampleCN: 每个线粒体都有自己的基因组。

items.example: Mitochondria divide independently of the cell cycle.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体可独立于细胞周期分裂。

items.example: Mitochondriopathy affects tissues that need much energy.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体病影响高耗能组织。

items.example: Cold exposure stimulates mitochondriogenesis in fat.
items.exampleCN: 寒冷刺激会促进脂肪中的线粒体生成。

items.example: Mitochondrial DNA has few repair enzymes.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体 DNA 的修复酶很少。

items.meaning: the inner compartment of the organelle
items.example: The matrix holds the enzymes of the citric acid cycle.
items.exampleCN: 基质容纳三羧酸循环的酶。

latinEntries.meaning: womb; a mould; the ground substance

definition_zh: 向上；起来；在上面；（数量）上升；（时间）到；完成；沿……而上
definition_en: towards a higher place, position, or level, or into an active or finished state
core_image: 一只手从低处把东西往上托
scene: 工地上吊绳绷紧，一捆钢筋从坑底慢慢露出地面。 The load came up out of the pit slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 up 是「向上」（第 1 个义项：由低处升高处）；句意为那捆货从坑底慢慢升上来。一只手从低处把东西往上托，正是这个词的核心。

pos.zh: 向上；起来
沿……而上；在……上面
向上的；已完成的；醒着的

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加比较级词尾构成，义为「上部的；较高的」
由 up 加 -ward 构成，义为「向上的；朝上」
由 up 与 stairs 复合，义为「在楼上；上楼」
由 up 与 set 复合，原义「打翻」，引申为「使心烦」

senses.title: Towards a higher place
senses.definition: towards a higher place or position
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的地方或位置
senses.example: She looked up at the clock and frowned.
senses.exampleCN: 她抬头看了看钟，皱起眉头。
senses.why: The word began as a Germanic adverb of upward motion, and that physical direction is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是日耳曼语中表示向上运动的副词，这一物理方向至今仍是它的中心。

senses.title: Into a standing or active state
senses.definition: into a standing, awake, or working state
senses.definitionCN: 进入站起、醒着或运转的状态
senses.example: He got up as soon as the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 铃声一响他就站了起来。
senses.why: Rising from the ground is also rising into activity, so standing up and waking up share one word.
senses.whyCN: 从地面升起也就是进入活动状态，因此「站起来」与「醒来」共用一个词。

senses.title: Along a road or a slope
senses.definition: used as a preposition for movement along or higher on something
senses.definitionCN: 作介词，表示沿某物前行或在其较高处
senses.example: They walked up the hill without speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一言不发地走上山坡。
senses.why: Walking up a slope is the same upward motion, so the adverb easily becomes a preposition of route.
senses.whyCN: 沿坡行走还是同一个向上的动作，因此这个副词很容易转为表示路径的介词。

senses.title: Increasing in number or level
senses.definition: used of prices, numbers, or levels that rise
senses.definitionCN: 用于价格、数字或水平的升高
senses.example: Sales went up sharply in the last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 上季度销量急剧上升。
senses.why: Numbers move in space in everyday speech, so a rising figure is simply a thing that goes up.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法里数字也在空间中移动，于是数值上升就是一样东西「往上去了」。

senses.title: Finished or out of time
senses.definition: used when a period or supply has come to its end
senses.definitionCN: 表示一段时间或供给已经到尽头
senses.example: Time is up, so put your pens down.
senses.exampleCN: 时间到了，把笔放下吧。
senses.why: A measure filled to the top can rise no further, and that image gives the sense of finished.
senses.whyCN: 容器装到顶就再升不上去了，这个意象生出「结束、用完」的意思。

senses.title: As far as a stated number
senses.definition: used with to for the greatest number reached
senses.definitionCN: 与 to 连用，表示所达到的最大数目
senses.example: The hall holds up to three hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅最多能容纳三百人。
senses.why: If up means reaching a point higher on a scale, then up to names the point where a number stops.
senses.whyCN: 既然 up 指沿某一刻度到达更高处，那么 up to 就指出数字停下的那一点。

intro.en: One of the oldest words in English, an adverb of place before it was anything else.
intro.cn: 英语中最古老的词之一，它首先是表示方位的副词。

items.en: The reconstructed form upp means up, and it has relatives in Dutch and German.
items.cn: 重构形式 upp 意为「向上」，在荷兰语和德语中都有同源词。

items.en: The adverb up is recorded early, with the comparative upper forming alongside it.
items.cn: 副词 up 很早就有记录，比较级 upper 也随之形成。

items.en: It is used with verbs of motion, as in standan up, to stand up.
items.cn: 它常与运动动词连用，如 standan up（站起来）。

items.en: Everyday phrases such as get up and up to now fix the word as a particle.
items.cn: get up、up to now 这类日常短语把它固定为小品词。

items.en: The sense of finished or used up appears in time is up and the gas is up.
items.cn: 「结束、用完」的含义出现在 time is up 与 the gas is up 这类说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives of up, while the near-meaning group compares direction and degree words.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 up 的复合词与派生词，近义组比较方向与程度词。

entries.definition: higher of two things
entries.definitionCN: 上面的；较高的

entries.definition: moving towards a higher point
entries.definitionCN: 向上的

entries.definition: on or to a higher floor
entries.definitionCN: 在楼上；上楼

entries.definition: on top of
entries.definitionCN: 在……之上

entries.definition: in a higher position
entries.definitionCN: 在……上方

entries.definition: across or higher than
entries.definitionCN: 越过；在上方

entries.definition: towards a lower place
entries.definitionCN: 向下

entries.definition: high in the air
entries.definitionCN: 在高处

normalIntro.en: A tiny word with a very long history, best learned through its verb phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 一个历史极悠久的小词，最好的记法是通过它与动词组成的短语。

normal.en: Learn up through verbs: get up, look up, stand up, give up.
normal.cn: 通过动词记：get up、look up、stand up、give up。

normal.en: Up plus to means as far as, either in number or in time.
normal.cn: up 加 to 意为「达到」，可用于数目或时间。

normal.en: Upper is the older comparative of up, not a separate root.
normal.cn: upper 是 up 较古老的比较级，并非另一个词根。

normal.en: Up and down together make the picture of repeated movement.
normal.cn: up and down 连用画出反复移动的画面。

normal.en: Time is up uses up as finished, not as direction.
normal.cn: time is up 里的 up 表示「结束」，不是方向。

abstract.en: Watch a hand lift something out of a pit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把东西从坑里托出来。

abstract.en: Feel a rope tighten and a bucket rise.
abstract.cn: 体会绳子绷紧、桶子升起。

abstract.en: See a hand switch a lamp on.
abstract.cn: 看一只手把灯打开。

examples.en: The children ran up the hill to see the sea.
examples.cn: 孩子们跑上山去看海。

examples.en: Prices went up again in the spring.
examples.cn: 价格在春天又一次上涨。

examples.en: Time is up, and the exam papers must be handed in.
examples.cn: 时间到了，试卷必须交上来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普」——搬东西时喊着阿普阿普，众人一起用力把重物往上抬。

root: 古英语 up（副词），源自日耳曼语重构形式 upp，与荷兰语 op、德语 auf 同源，本义「向上」

sensesIntro.en: One upward motion supplies direction, then standing, then rising levels, finally finishing and reaching a limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个向上的动作先给方向，再给站立，再给上升，最后给结束与达到极限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifting something from below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从下面把东西抬起。

branches.en: The direction branch: eyes and objects go higher.
branches.cn: 方向分支：视线与物件往高处去。

branches.en: The state branch: up means awake, standing, working.
branches.cn: 状态分支：up 指醒着、站着、运转着。

branches.en: The preposition branch: along or higher on a road.
branches.cn: 介词分支：沿路而行或位于高处。

branches.en: The figure branch: numbers that keep climbing.
branches.cn: 数字分支：一路往上爬的数值。

branches.en: The limit branch: used up, and as far as a number.
branches.cn: 极限分支：用完了，以及达到某个数目。

intro.en: A bare Germanic adverb that now works as particle, preposition, adjective, and noun.
intro.cn: 一个光秃秃的日耳曼语副词，如今可作小品词、介词、形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin expresses the same direction with sursum, upward, and the prefix super-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 sursum（向上）与前缀 super- 表达同一方向。

items.example: The balloon went up.
items.exampleCN: 气球升了上去。

items.example: The upper shelf is empty.
items.exampleCN: 上层架子是空的。

items.example: Up gives upward.
items.exampleCN: up 加它成为 upward。

items.example: She went upstairs.
items.exampleCN: 她上楼去了。

items.example: The news upset him.
items.exampleCN: 这消息让他心烦。

items.example: Up to ten people came.
items.exampleCN: 来了多达十人。

items.example: The boat turned upside down.
items.exampleCN: 船翻了。

items.example: Update the list.
items.exampleCN: 更新名单。

items.meaning: to raise to a better level
items.example: They upgraded the system.
items.exampleCN: 他们升级了系统。

items.example: The music uplifted her.
items.exampleCN: 这音乐让她振奋。

definition_zh: 计算的；与计算有关的；借助计算机完成的；计算代价与复杂度的；计算模型与仿真的；以计算方法命名的学科的；数值误差与计算精度的；认知科学中「心智即计算」的
definition_en: relating to calculation, or describing work that is carried out by methods of calculation and often by machines
core_image: 一张网格纸被切成无数小格，每一格同时被算过一遍
scene: 实验室的墙上贴着一张被切成许多小方格的网格纸，每一格都标着一个步骤。 Their computational approach splits the image into small patches and scores each one.
sceneCN: 这里 computational 指「属于计算模型与仿真方法的」（第 4 个义项：以计算模型处理问题）；句意：他们的计算式方法把图像切成小块，再逐块打分。图中可辨识物件：网格纸、小方格、步骤标号、屏幕、放大镜。

pos.zh: 计算的；与计算有关的

derivatives.zh: 计算；计算结果
在计算方面；从计算角度
可计算性（罕用）
计算
计算机
可计算的

senses.title: Belonging to calculation in general
senses.definition: relating to calculation itself, whether done by hand, by formula or by machine
senses.definitionCN: 与计算本身有关，不论计算由手工、公式还是机器完成
senses.example: The paper keeps the computational part separate from the field study.
senses.exampleCN: 论文把计算部分与实地研究分开处理。
senses.why: The suffix -al simply says 'of or belonging to', so the adjective can attach to calculation without naming any device.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 只表示「属于」，因此这个形容词可以挂在计算上，而不提任何装置。

senses.title: Done with a machine rather than by hand
senses.definition: carried out by machine methods instead of manual or purely theoretical work
senses.definitionCN: 以机器方法而非手工或纯理论方式完成的
senses.example: A computational shortcut saved the team weeks of laboratory work.
senses.exampleCN: 一条计算捷径为团队省下了数周的实验室工作。
senses.why: Once most long calculations moved to machines, the adjective became a practical label for the machine route.
senses.whyCN: 当长串计算大多转到机器上，这个形容词就成了机器路线的实用标签。

senses.title: The price of running an algorithm
senses.titleCN: 运行算法要付出的代价
senses.definition: the time, memory or number of steps that an algorithm costs as its input grows
senses.definitionCN: 算法随输入增大而耗费的时间、内存或步骤数
senses.example: The team measured the computational cost before scaling up.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在扩大规模之前先测量了计算成本。
senses.why: If a method is to be judged practical, its demands need a name, and that name is the adjective attached to cost or complexity.
senses.whyCN: 要判断一种方法是否实用，就得给它的开销一个名字，这名字就是挂在成本或复杂度前的这个形容词。

senses.title: Models and simulation
senses.definition: describing a model or simulation that represents a system by rules a machine can run
senses.definitionCN: 形容用机器可执行的规则来表征某个系统的模型或仿真
senses.example: A computational model of the climate ran a century in an afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一个气候计算模型在一个下午里跑完了一百年。
senses.why: A model becomes computational when its behaviour is produced by step-by-step calculation rather than by physical resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 当一个模型的行为由逐步计算产生、而非靠实物相似，它就是计算模型。

senses.title: A discipline named by its method
senses.definition: used in the names of fields, such as computational linguistics or computational biology, that apply calculation to another subject
senses.definitionCN: 用于学科名称，如计算语言学或计算生物学，表示把计算应用到另一门学问
senses.example: The field of computational linguistics borrows tools from statistics and grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 计算语言学借用了统计与语法的工具。
senses.why: When a field is defined by its method rather than its subject, the adjective moves in front of the subject name and stays there.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学问靠方法而非题材定义，这个形容词就移到题材名前面并固定下来。

senses.title: Thinking in steps a machine could follow
senses.titleCN: 按机器能照做的步骤思考
senses.definition: describing the kind of problem solving that breaks a task into ordered steps, decomposition and abstraction
senses.definitionCN: 形容把任务拆成有序步骤、分解与抽象的问题解决方式
senses.example: Schools now teach computational thinking before any programming language.
senses.exampleCN: 学校现在先教计算思维，再教任何编程语言。
senses.why: The adjective reaches beyond machinery to a habit of mind, because the same ordered steps can be taught without a device.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词越出机器，指向一种思维习惯，因为同一套有序步骤不用设备也能教。

senses.title: Error and precision in numbers
senses.definition: relating to the rounding, truncation and instability that arise when calculation is done with finite precision
senses.definitionCN: 与有限精度计算中出现的舍入、截断与不稳定性有关
senses.example: Each extra step added a computational error to the total.
senses.exampleCN: 每多一步，总数里就多一份计算误差。
senses.why: Machines work with limited digits, so the adjective also marks the flaws that calculation introduces into an answer.
senses.whyCN: 机器只有有限的位数，因此这个形容词也标记计算给答案引入的缺陷。

senses.title: The mind described as calculation
senses.definition: in cognitive science, holding that mental processes are operations on representations, in the manner of a calculation
senses.definitionCN: 在认知科学中主张心理过程是对表征的运算，其方式如同计算
senses.example: Some psychologists defend a computational view of memory.
senses.exampleCN: 一些心理学家为记忆的计算观辩护。
senses.why: If the mind performs operations on symbols, then every mental theory built on that picture can carry the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 如果心灵对符号执行运算，那么建立在这幅图景上的每一种心智理论都能带这个形容词。

intro.en: Computational is computation plus the adjective suffix -al, from Latin -alis. Computation descends from Latin computatio, a noun of action from computare 'to reckon together'. The adjective became common only in the twentieth century, with the growth of numerical methods and machine calculation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computational 由 computation 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，-al 出自拉丁 -alis。computation 出自拉丁 computatio，是 computare「一起核算」的动作名词。这个形容词到二十世纪才随数值方法与机器计算的兴起而通行。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare 'to reckon, think' is the root; repute, dispute and impute share it.
items.cn: putare「核算、思考」是词根；repute、dispute 与 impute 共用它。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare made computare, 'to reckon together', the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare「合起来核算」，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Computatio was the action noun 'a reckoning', formed with -io from the same verb.
items.cn: computatio 是动作名词「核算」，由同一动词加 -io 构成。

items.en: -alis was the ordinary Latin suffix for 'belonging to', and it becomes -al in English adjectives such as national and natural.
items.cn: -alis 是拉丁语里表示「属于」的常用后缀，在英语形容词里变成 -al，如 national 与 natural。

items.en: English took computation through French in the Middle Ages, at first for any reckoning or account.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪经法语引入 computation，最初泛指任何核算或账目。

items.en: Computational spread with numerical analysis and machine calculation, then into field names; first citation uncertain: the earliest English use of the adjective is not securely dated.
items.cn: computational 随数值分析与机器计算传播，后来又进入学科名；首见年代不确定：这个形容词最早的英语用例年代没有可靠定论。

note.en: Group one is the compute family: the noun, the device, the verb and the possibility all look alike but play different roles. Group two holds adjectives that describe how a result was obtained.
note.cn: 第一组是 compute 词族：名词、设备、动词与可能性外形相似，却各扮不同角色。第二组是描述结果如何获得的形容词。

entries.definition: A single calculation or its result, countable when it means one run and uncountable as a process.
entries.definitionCN: 一次计算或其结果；指一次运行时可数，指过程时不可数。

entries.definition: The countable machine; the adjective never points at a machine directly.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的机器；这个形容词从不直接指向某台机器。

entries.definition: To carry out a calculation; the adjective is the description built on the noun, not on the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计算；这个形容词是建立在名词而非动词上的描述。

entries.definition: Able to be calculated in principle; it judges a problem, while computational describes a method.
entries.definitionCN: 原则上可被算出；它判断问题，而 computational 描述方法。

entries.definition: Carried out by approximating with numbers, often in contrast to an exact symbolic solution.
entries.definitionCN: 以数值近似来完成，常与精确的符号解相对。

entries.definition: Defined by a step-by-step procedure, whether or not a machine runs it.
entries.definitionCN: 由逐步程序来定义，不论是否由机器执行。

entries.definition: Belonging to mathematics at large, of which calculation is only one part.
entries.definitionCN: 属于整个数学，计算只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: Produced as an imitation of a real system; it describes the output rather than the calculating method.
entries.definitionCN: 作为真实系统的模仿产物；描述输出而非计算方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the -al adjective, the cost and complexity of algorithms, and the field names built on the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-al 形容词、算法的时间与复杂度代价，以及用这个词构造的学科名。

normal.en: Computation plus -al: of or belonging to calculation.
normal.cn: computation 加 -al：属于计算的。

normal.en: It describes the method, never the machine itself.
normal.cn: 它描述方法，从不直接描述机器本身。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: computational model, computational cost, computational linguistics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：计算模型、计算成本、计算语言学。

normal.en: The adverb form is computationally, as in computationally cheap.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 computationally，如「计算上开销小」。

normal.en: Limit states are more and most computational, not -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级用 more 与 most，不用 -er 与 -est。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of graph paper cut into a thousand squares, each worked through at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方格纸被切成一千格，每一格同时被算一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a stopwatch running beside an algorithm as the input doubles.
abstract.cn: 想象输入翻倍时，一只秒表在算法旁边计时。

abstract.en: Picture a mind drawn as arrows moving between small labelled boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象把心灵画成在许多带标签的小方框之间移动的箭头。

examples.en: The two approaches differ in their computational demands, not in their aims.
examples.cn: 两种路径的差别在计算需求上，而不在目标上。

examples.en: A computational model can fail for reasons that no experiment would reveal.
examples.cn: 计算模型可能因为实验无法揭示的原因而失败。

examples.en: Her argument turns on a computational account of how sentences are parsed.
examples.cn: 她的论证关键在于一套关于句子如何被解析的计算解释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「comput（算）+ ation（行为）+ al（的）」——属于计算那一套的：计算的、计算式的

root: computation + -al；computation 出自拉丁 computatio「核算」，computatio 又出自 computare「一起核算」= com-「一起」+ putare「核算」。同根词有 compute、computer、computable、computationally。形容词义在二十世纪随数值方法与机器计算通行。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: belonging to calculation, done by machine, the cost of an algorithm, a model that runs, a field named by its method, an ordered habit of thought, the error of finite precision and the mind treated as calculation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个形容词：属于计算、由机器完成、算法的代价、能跑起来的模型、以方法命名的学科、有序的思维习惯、有限精度带来的误差，以及被当成计算的心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the quality of being produced by step-by-step calculation rather than by direct observation.
core.cn: 核心意象：由逐步计算产生、而非由直接观察得来的那种性质。

branches.en: FROM BELONGING TO DOING: the general 'of calculation' sense narrows into 'done by machine' once machines take over the work.
branches.cn: 从归属到执行：泛泛的「属于计算」在机器接手后收窄为「由机器完成」。

branches.en: THE PRICE TAG: every method has a cost in time and memory, and the adjective names that cost.
branches.cn: 代价标签：每种方法都有时间与内存上的开销，这个形容词就给这份开销命名。

branches.en: THE MODEL THAT RUNS: a representation becomes computational when rules, not resemblance, produce its behaviour.
branches.cn: 会跑的模型：当行为由规则而非相似性产生，一个表征就成了计算模型。

branches.en: METHOD INTO NAME: the adjective prefixes whole disciplines, and then hardens into a way of thinking taught on its own.
branches.cn: 方法变成名称：这个形容词加到整门学科前面，随后凝固成一种可单独教授的思维方式。

branches.en: FLAW AND THEORY: finite digits leave error in the answer, while the same picture of stepwise operations becomes a theory of mind.
branches.cn: 缺陷与理论：有限的位数给答案留下误差，而同一幅逐步运算的图景又成了心智理论。

intro.en: Computational stacks a Latin root, a Latin action-noun ending and a Latin adjective ending; each layer is productive in English.
intro.cn: computational 叠了一个拉丁词根、一个拉丁动作名词词尾与一个拉丁形容词词尾，每一层在英语里都能产词。

latinIntro.en: Putare 'to reckon' yields computare and then computatio; -alis 'belonging to' gives English -al, which turns the noun into an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: putare「核算」生出 computare，再出 computatio；-alis「属于」给出英语 -al，把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The prefix gathers the figures into one sum.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数字聚成一个总和。

items.example: Counting and judging grow from one root.
items.exampleCN: 计数与判断从同一个词根长出。

items.example: The verb supplies the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词供给整个英语词族。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of computation.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是 computation 的基础。

items.meaning: relating to; of the kind of
items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基础。

items.example: The model is computational rather than physical.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型是计算的，而非实物的。

items.example: The method is computationally expensive.
items.exampleCN: 这种方法在计算上很昂贵。

items.example: The term computationality is rare in ordinary use.
items.exampleCN: computationality 在日常使用中很罕见。

items.example: Machines compute far faster than people.
items.exampleCN: 机器算得比人快得多。

definition_zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占
definition_en: exclusive control of a market or commodity by a single seller
core_image: 一条街只有一家店开门，橱窗上贴着唯一的价目表，顾客排成长队也别无选择
scene: 小镇上唯一的一家加油站挂出新的价目牌，排队的车主只能接受。 A local monopoly can raise prices until customers travel to a distant substitute.
sceneCN: 这里 monopoly 指「由单一卖方控制的市场结构」（第 1 个义项：市场上只有一个卖方）；句意为地方性垄断可以把价格提高，直到顾客愿意去远处寻找替代品。图中可辨识物件：唯一的加油站、单一价目牌、排队车辆、远处的替代站点。

pos.zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占

derivatives.zh: 垄断；独占

senses.title: A market with one seller
senses.definition: a market structure in which a single seller supplies the whole demand and faces no direct rival
senses.definitionCN: 由单一卖方供应全部需求、没有直接对手的市场结构
senses.example: The island's ferry service is a monopoly with no alternative route.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的渡轮服务是一种没有替代航线的垄断。
senses.why: monos 'single' plus polein 'sell' gives the literal reading: one seller for the whole market.
senses.whyCN: monos「单一」加 polein「卖」给出字面读法：整个市场只有一个卖方。

senses.title: An exclusive right granted by law
senses.definition: a legal privilege allowing one party alone to trade in a good or service
senses.definitionCN: 允许某一方独自经营某种商品或服务的法定特权
senses.example: The old charter gave the company a monopoly on salt.
senses.exampleCN: 旧特许状给了这家公司食盐的专营权。
senses.why: the Greek word first named a concession granted by a city, so the legal sense is older than the economic one.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初指城邦授予的特许，因此法律义比经济义更早。

senses.title: The commodity under exclusive control
senses.definition: the good or service that only one supplier is allowed or able to provide
senses.definitionCN: 只允许或只能够由一家供应商提供的商品或服务
senses.example: Broadcasting was once a monopoly of the state.
senses.exampleCN: 广播曾经是国家独占的事业。
senses.why: English allows the word to stand for the thing controlled, not only for the control itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个词指被控制的对象，而不只是控制本身。

senses.title: The firm that holds the market
senses.definition: the company or organization that enjoys exclusive control
senses.definitionCN: 享有独占控制权的公司或机构
senses.example: Regulators treated the railway as a monopoly and capped its fares.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者把这家铁路公司当作垄断企业，并限制其票价。
senses.why: metonymy turns the structure into the actor, so monopoly can mean the monopolist.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把结构变成行为者，于是 monopoly 可以指垄断企业。

senses.title: A state monopoly
senses.definition: exclusive government control of a trade, often for revenue or public order
senses.definitionCN: 政府对某项贸易的独占控制，常用于增加财政收入或维护公共秩序
senses.example: The tobacco monopoly supplies a large share of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 烟草专卖提供了预算的很大一部分。
senses.why: early modern states used exclusive grants as a tax-collecting device, and the phrase kept that association.
senses.whyCN: 近代早期国家把专营特许当作征税工具，这个说法保留了这层联系。

senses.title: A temporary monopoly from a patent
senses.titleCN: 专利或版权带来的暂时独占
senses.definition: exclusive commercial use of an invention or work for a limited term
senses.definitionCN: 在有限期限内对某项发明或作品的独占商业使用
senses.example: The patent gave the maker a monopoly for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 专利给了制造商二十年的独占期。
senses.why: intellectual property is a deliberate, time-limited monopoly meant to reward disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 知识产权是一种有意设置、期限有限的垄断，用以奖励公开。

senses.title: A natural monopoly
senses.definition: a market where high fixed costs make one supplier cheaper than several
senses.definitionCN: 固定成本很高、使一家供应比多家供应更便宜的市场
senses.example: Water pipes form a natural monopoly because duplicating them is wasteful.
senses.exampleCN: 水管构成自然垄断，因为重复铺设是浪费。
senses.why: economists call it natural because the single supplier arises from cost structure, not from a legal grant.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家称之为「自然」，因为单一供应来自成本结构，而非法律授予。

senses.title: Exclusive possession of anything
senses.titleCN: 对任何事物的排他性掌控（比喻义）
senses.definition: complete control of a thing or topic so that others have no share
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或话题的完全控制，使他人无从分享
senses.example: The city does not have a monopoly on good ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 好主意并非这座城市所独占。
senses.why: detached from trade, the word keeps only its core of being the sole holder.
senses.whyCN: 脱离贸易语境后，这个词只保留「唯一持有者」这一核心。

intro.en: Monopoly comes from Greek monopōlion 'exclusive right to sell', built on monos 'alone' and pōlein 'to sell', and enters English through Latin monopolium. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monopoly 来自希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」，由 monos「单独」与 pōlein「卖」构成，经拉丁 monopolium 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos meant 'alone, single'. The same element opens monologue, monorail and monarchy, where it combines with different second terms.
items.cn: monos 意为「单独的、唯一的」。同一成分出现在 monologue、monorail 与 monarchy 的开头，与不同的第二成分组合。

items.en: Pōlein meant 'to sell'. The -poly of monopoly is this verb, not Greek polys 'many', and it has nothing to do with polis 'city'.
items.cn: pōlein 意为「卖」。monopoly 中的 -poly 是这个动词，而非希腊语 polys「多」，也与 polis「城邦」无关。

items.en: Monopōlion named an exclusive sale or a concession granted by a city, especially the right to sell a particular commodity.
items.cn: monopōlion 指独家售卖或城邦授予的特许，尤其是经营某种商品的专权。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as monopolium and used it for exclusive trading rights, including grants made by rulers.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词吸收为 monopolium，用于独家贸易权，包括统治者授予的特许。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century, first for royal grants and later for any single-seller market as economics developed.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个词，先指王室特许，随着经济学发展又指任何单一卖方市场。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. The deeper origin of pōlein is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。pōlein 的更深来源属重构形式，并非有直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring market structures whose Greek second elements are often confused; group two holds words for control or exclusive dealing that are not market structures.
note.cn: 第一组是第二成分常被混淆的邻近市场结构；第二组是表示控制或独家交易、但并非市场结构的词。

entries.definition: A market with a single buyer; its Greek second element is opsōnein 'to buy', so it is the mirror image of monopoly.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个买方的市场；其希腊第二成分是 opsōnein「买」，因此是 monopoly 的镜像。

entries.definition: A market dominated by a small number of sellers; the second element is the same verb 'to sell', but the first is oligos 'few'.
entries.definitionCN: 由少数卖方支配的市场；第二成分同为「卖」这个动词，但第一成分是 oligos「少数」。

entries.definition: A market with two dominant sellers, built with Latin duo- on the same Greek selling element.
entries.definitionCN: 由两家主要卖方构成的市场，以拉丁 duo- 接同一个希腊「卖」成分。

entries.definition: The person or firm that holds a monopoly; the structure is monopoly, while the holder is the monopolist.
entries.definitionCN: 持有垄断地位的人或企业；结构是 monopoly，持有者则是 monopolist。

entries.definition: To gain control of a commodity by buying enough of it to dictate price; it is an action, not a market structure.
entries.definitionCN: 通过买下足够多的商品来控制价格；它是一种行为，而非市场结构。

entries.definition: The state of being restricted to one party; a monopoly is one legal or economic form of exclusivity.
entries.definitionCN: 仅限一方享有的状态；垄断是排他性的一种法律或经济形式。

entries.definition: An agreement among independent sellers to fix prices or divide markets; it imitates monopoly without a single seller.
entries.definitionCN: 独立卖方之间固定价格或划分市场的协议；它模仿垄断，却没有单一卖方。

entries.definition: In late nineteenth-century law, a trust was a combination of firms placed under shared trustees, the target of early antitrust law.
entries.definitionCN: 在 19 世纪后期的法律中，trust 指置于共同受托人下的企业联合，是早期反垄断法的对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monos 'single' + polein 'sell': one seller for the whole market.
normal.cn: monos「单一」+ polein「卖」：整个市场只有一个卖方。

normal.en: The family runs monopoly, monopolist, monopolize, monopolistic, monopolization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monopoly、monopolist、monopolize、monopolistic、monopolization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: natural monopoly, state monopoly, monopoly power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：自然垄断、国家专卖、垄断力量。

normal.en: The -poly here is 'sell', not 'many': oligopoly and duopoly use the same verb.
normal.cn: 这里的 -poly 是「卖」而非「多」：oligopoly 与 duopoly 用的是同一个动词。

normal.en: Its mirror image is monopsony, where one buyer faces many sellers.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是 monopsony，即一个买方面对许多卖方。

abstract.en: Picture a street with one lit window and a queue outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，门外排着队。

abstract.en: Picture a single key that opens every door in a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙能打开一栋楼里的每一扇门。

abstract.en: Picture one price tag that nobody on the street can undercut.
abstract.cn: 想象一张街上无人能压低的价签。

examples.en: The government broke up the monopoly after a decade of complaints.
examples.cn: 在十年投诉之后，政府拆分了这家垄断企业。

examples.en: A patent is a legal monopoly limited in time and scope.
examples.cn: 专利是一种在时间与范围上受限的法定垄断。

examples.en: No single company should have a monopoly on the public record.
examples.cn: 不应由任何一家公司独占公共记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mono（单一）+ poly（卖）」——整个市场只有一家在卖 → 垄断

root: 希腊 monos「单独」+ pōlein「卖」→ 希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」→ 拉丁 monopolium → 英语 monopoly。此处的 -poly 是「卖」，与 polys「多」及 polis「城邦」无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one seller: a single hand holds the whole supply, and that hold is then seen as a market structure, a legal grant, the commodity, the firm, a state trade, a patent term, a cost-driven case, and finally any exclusive possession.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个卖方展开：一只手握住全部供给，这个握有再依次被视为市场结构、法律授予、被控商品、企业本身、国家贸易、专利期限、成本造成的特例，最后是任何排他性占有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lit shop window on a street, with a queue that has nowhere else to go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，队伍无处可去。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND ACTOR: the single-seller market, and the firm that occupies it.
branches.cn: 结构与行为者：单一卖方市场，以及占据它的企业。

branches.en: GRANT AND OBJECT: a legal privilege, and the commodity that privilege covers.
branches.cn: 授予与对象：一项法律特权，以及该特权覆盖的商品。

branches.en: THE STATE: the same exclusive hold exercised for revenue or order.
branches.cn: 国家：为财政收入或秩序行使的同一种独占。

branches.en: TIME-LIMITED AND COST-DRIVEN: a patent term, and a market where fixed costs favour one supplier.
branches.cn: 限期与成本驱动：专利期限，以及固定成本偏向单一卖方的市场。

branches.en: ANY EXCLUSIVE HOLD: the word detached from trade and used for ideas or records.
branches.cn: 任何独占：脱离贸易后被用于思想或记录的词。

intro.en: Monopoly is a Greek compound filtered through Latin, so its two Greek elements can be read apart, and English then built a whole family on the noun.
intro.cn: monopoly 是经拉丁语过滤的希腊复合词，因此两个希腊成分可以分开读，英语随后又在这个名词上建起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin monopolium carries the Greek compound into English; the family then adds -ist, -ize and -ation, while monopsony replaces the selling element with a buying one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monopolium 把这个希腊复合词带入英语；词族随后加 -ist、-ize 与 -ation，而 monopsony 把「卖」的成分换成「买」。

items.example: The element also opens monologue and monorail.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 monologue 与 monorail 的开头。

items.example: The selling element is shared by oligopoly and duopoly.
items.exampleCN: 这个「卖」的成分由 oligopoly 与 duopoly 共享。

items.example: A local monopoly raised prices without fear.
items.exampleCN: 一家地方垄断者无所顾忌地提价。

items.example: The monopolist owned every pipeline in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这家垄断企业拥有谷地里的每一条管道。
