senses.title: Belonging to numbers
senses.titleCN: 数字的：与数字本身有关
senses.definition: relating to numbers as such, or to the system of counting and calculation
senses.definitionCN: 与数字本身或计数与计算体系有关
senses.example: The keyboard layout follows a numerical system, not an alphabetical one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个键盘布局遵循数字体系，而不是字母体系。
senses.why: The adjective marks the domain: the subject is numbers, so questions of value, order, and amount all belong here.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出领域：主题是数字，因此值、顺序与数量的问题都归在这里。

senses.title: Expressed as a number
senses.titleCN: 用数字表示：不写形容词，只写数
senses.definition: given in the form of a number rather than a word or a symbol
senses.definitionCN: 以数字而非词语或符号的形式给出
senses.example: The rating is numerical, from one to ten, with no verbal comment.
senses.exampleCN: 评分是数值型的，从一到十，不附文字评语。
senses.why: Here the word contrasts forms of expression: the same fact could be said in words, but a numerical form allows counting and comparison.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词对比表达形式：同一事实可以用文字说，但数值形式便于计数与比较。

senses.title: A number attached to a quantity
senses.definition: the particular number that expresses the size of a quantity in stated units
senses.definitionCN: 在给定单位下表示某一量大小的具体数字
senses.example: The numerical value of the coefficient depends on the units chosen.
senses.exampleCN: 该系数的数值取决于所选单位。
senses.why: A quantity has a size, and numerical names the number that reports it; change the unit and the number changes while the quantity does not.
senses.whyCN: 一个量有大小，numerical 指的是报告它大小的那个数；换单位，数会变，量本身不变。

senses.title: Ordered by number
senses.titleCN: 按数字排序：一二三四排下去
senses.definition: arranged according to number rather than by name, date, or topic
senses.definitionCN: 按数字而非名称、日期或主题排列
senses.example: The files are stored in numerical order from 001 to 999.
senses.exampleCN: 这些档案按 001 到 999 的数字顺序存放。
senses.why: Numbers provide a sequence that needs no interpretation: once the rule is fixed, anyone can find where an item belongs.
senses.whyCN: 数字提供一种无须解释的次序：规则一旦固定，任何人都能找到某物该放哪儿。

senses.title: Strength in count, not skill
senses.titleCN: 数量优势：人多，而非更强
senses.definition: advantage that comes from having more people or units than an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 因人数或单位数量多于对手而取得的优势
senses.example: The defenders had numerical superiority but no better position.
senses.exampleCN: 防守方在人数上占优，但地形并不更好。
senses.why: In military and competitive settings, numerical compares counts rather than quality, and the word admits that quantity can decide even without skill.
senses.whyCN: 在军事与竞赛语境里，numerical 比较的是数量而非质量；这个词承认数量有时无须技巧也能决定胜负。

senses.title: Solved by calculation
senses.titleCN: 数值方法：用近似计算求解
senses.definition: describing methods that approximate solutions by repeated calculation rather than exact algebra
senses.definitionCN: 指通过反复计算逼近解，而非求出精确代数解的方法
senses.example: The weather model uses numerical methods to step the atmosphere forward.
senses.exampleCN: 天气模型用数值方法把大气状态一步步向前推进。
senses.why: When equations cannot be solved exactly, calculation replaces derivation; numerical marks that the answer is an approximation built from many small steps.
senses.whyCN: 当方程无法精确求解时，计算取代推导；numerical 标出答案是由许多小步凑出的近似。

senses.title: Data in number form
senses.titleCN: 数值数据：能进表格的那种资料
senses.definition: information recorded as measurements or counts and therefore open to arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 以测量值或计数记录、因而可作算术处理的信息
senses.example: The study combined numerical data with interviews of the same families.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把数值数据与对同一批家庭的访谈结合起来。
senses.why: Data becomes numerical when it has been given units and a scale, which is what allows it to be averaged, plotted, and tested.
senses.whyCN: 数据在被赋予单位与标度后才成为数值数据，也正因如此才能求平均、绘图与检验。

senses.title: Machine control by numbers
senses.titleCN: 数控：让机器照着数字走
senses.definition: describing the control of a machine by coded numerical instructions rather than by a hand-operated lever
senses.definitionCN: 指用编码数字指令而非手动操纵杆控制机器
senses.example: The workshop replaced its manual lathes with numerical control machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家车间用数控机床取代了手动车床。
senses.why: The word entered manufacturing because a path can be described as a list of coordinates; numbers then become the instructions a tool follows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入制造业，是因为一条路径可以写成一组坐标；数字由此成为刀具遵循的指令。

intro.en: Numerical comes from Latin numerus, a number, through the adjective numericus and the English suffix -al. The same root gives numeral, numerous, and enumerate.
intro.cn: numerical 来自拉丁语 numerus“数字”，经形容词 numericus 与英语后缀 -al 构成。同一词根还给出 numeral、numerous、enumerate。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count, a measure, and also a rhythm or a place in a series.
items.cn: numerus 意为数字、计数、度量，也可指节奏或序列中的位置。

items.en: The verb meant to count or to reckon. It is the source of English enumerate, to count out one by one.
items.cn: 动词意为计数、结算。它是英语 enumerate（逐一点数）的来源。

items.en: The adjective meant full of numbers, hence numerous or many. English numerous keeps only the 'many' sense.
items.cn: 该形容词意为“充满数字的”，因而表示“众多”。英语 numerous 只保留了“多”的意思。

items.en: Later Latin numericus meant concerned with numbers. It passed into learned English as numeric and numerical.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 numericus 意为“与数字有关的”，作为学术词进入英语，形成 numeric 与 numerical。

items.en: Numerical entered English through mathematical writing, where it distinguished quantity from shape, word, or symbol.
items.cn: numerical 经数学写作进入英语，用来把“数量”与形状、词语、符号区分开。

items.en: Computing and engineering widened the word to numerical methods, numerical data, and numerical control, where numbers serve as instructions.
items.cn: 计算与工程把该词扩展到数值方法、数值数据与数控；在这些领域，数字成了指令。

note.en: The first group is the number family; the second compares adjectives that describe measurement and quantity.
note.cn: 第一组是 number 词族；第二组比较描述度量与数量的形容词。

entries.definition: a count or symbol; or to count. It is the base noun behind all these forms.
entries.definitionCN: 计数或数字符号；也可作动词表示计数。它是这些形式背后的基础名词。

entries.definition: a written symbol for a number, such as 7 or VII. It names the mark, not the quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 表示数字的书写符号，如 7 或 VII；命名的是符号，不是数量。

entries.definition: another form of numerical, now especially common in computing and keypads.
entries.definitionCN: numerical 的另一种形式，今多用于计算机与键盘语境。

entries.definition: measured by amount rather than by quality. It describes a method, while numerical describes a form.
entries.definitionCN: 以数量而非性质来衡量；描述方法，而 numerical 描述形式。

entries.definition: represented by discrete digits, especially in electronics. It is about encoding, not arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 以离散数位表示，尤指电子领域；关乎编码，而非算术。

entries.definition: relating to the collection and analysis of data. It uses numbers but adds inference.
entries.definitionCN: 与数据收集和分析有关；使用数字，但增加了推断。

entries.definition: using figures of speech rather than literal numbers or plain meaning. It is the opposite direction from numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 使用修辞格而非字面数字或本义；与 numerical 方向相反。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin numerus, number, plus -ical, 'relating to'. Numerical simply means number-related.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 numerus“数字”，加 -ical“与……有关”。numerical 就是“与数字有关的”。

normal.en: Numerus is number; -ical is related to. Numerical equals number-related, nothing more.
normal.cn: numerus 是数字，-ical 是“与……有关”。numerical 就是“跟数字有关”，没有别的。

normal.en: A numerical report shows a row of values instead of a sentence of praise.
normal.cn: 数值报告给出一排数值，而不是一句赞美。

normal.en: Numerical order is the shelf where 001 always comes before 002.
normal.cn: 数字顺序就是 001 永远排在 002 前面的那种书架。

normal.en: Numerical superiority counts people, not skill.
normal.cn: 数量优势数的是人，不是本事。

normal.en: In a workshop, numerical control means the tool reads numbers and moves.
normal.cn: 在车间里，数控意味着刀具读了数字就移动。

abstract.en: A numerical answer hides its units; without units, the number is only a shape.
abstract.cn: 数值答案把单位藏在背后；没有单位，数字只是一个形状。

abstract.en: What can be made numerical can be compared, and what can be compared can be managed.
abstract.cn: 能变成数值的东西就能比较，能比较的东西就能被管理。

abstract.en: The word promises precision, but an approximation done in numbers is still an approximation.
abstract.cn: 这个词许诺精确，但用数字做出来的近似终究还是近似。

examples.en: The committee asked for a numerical estimate, not a general impression of the crowd.
examples.cn: 委员会要求给出人数估计，而不是对人群的笼统印象。

examples.en: Numerical models disagree with each other mainly in how they treat clouds.
examples.cn: 各数值模型之间的分歧主要在于如何处理云。

examples.en: The old milling machine was converted to numerical control to cut curved parts.
examples.cn: 那台旧铣床被改装成数控设备，用来切削曲面零件。

dict_mnemonic.text: numer（数字）+ ical（的）——满脑子都是数字，就是“数值的”。

root: 源自拉丁语 numerus（数字、计数），经 numericus 与英语后缀 -al 构成，本义为“与数字有关的”；同根词还有 numeral、numerous、enumerate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of numerical. All point to numbers, but the numbers play different roles: they can be the subject, the form of expression, the value of a quantity, a sequence, a count of people, a method of calculation, a kind of data, or instructions for a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: numerical 的八个义项都指向数字，但数字扮演的角色不同：它可以是主题、表达形式、某量的大小、排列次序、人数、计算方法、数据种类，或机器的指令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of small boxes, each holding a single digit, with no adjectives anywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面墙分成许多小格，每格只放一个数字，没有任何形容词。

chain: NUMBERS BECOME DATA, METHODS, AND INSTRUCTIONS

branches.en: NUMBERS AS SUBJECT AND FORM: the domain of number, and the choice to express a fact in digits.
branches.cn: 数字作主题与形式：数字的领域，以及选择用数位表达事实。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS VALUE AND ORDER: the size of a quantity, and the sequence on a shelf.
branches.cn: 数字作值与序：量的大小，以及架上的排列次序。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS COUNT: superiority that comes from having more units than the opponent.
branches.cn: 数字作计数：因单位多于对手而形成的优势。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS METHOD AND DATA: approximation by calculation, and measurements open to arithmetic.
branches.cn: 数字作方法与数据：以计算求近似，以及可作算术处理的测量值。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS COMMAND: coordinates read by a machine tool.
branches.cn: 数字作指令：机床读取的坐标。

intro.en: Numerical is numerus plus the adjective suffix -ical. The family runs through number, numeral, numerate, and the prefix e- in enumerate.
intro.cn: numerical 是 numerus 加形容词后缀 -ical。词族包括 number、numeral、numerate，以及带前缀 e- 的 enumerate。

latinIntro.en: The base is numerus, number or count, with the verb numerare and the adjective numerosus. Latin also used numerus for rhythm and rank.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 numerus“数字、计数”，另有动词 numerare 与形容词 numerosus。拉丁语还用 numerus 指节奏与等级。

items.meaning: a count, a symbol, or a quantity
items.example: The number of applicants doubled in one year.
items.exampleCN: 申请人数量一年内翻了一倍。

items.meaning: a symbol used to write a number
items.example: Roman numerals use letters instead of digits.
items.exampleCN: 罗马数字用字母而非数位。

items.meaning: relating to numbers or expressed by them
items.meaningCN: 与数字有关的，或以数字表示的
items.example: The table gives numerical results for each trial.
items.exampleCN: 表格给出每次试验的数值结果。

items.meaning: in number or in numerical terms
items.example: The two groups were numerically equal.
items.exampleCN: 两个群体在人数上相等。

items.meaning: able to work with numbers; also to count
items.meaningCN: 会算数的；也可作动词表示计数
items.example: A numerate reader can check the totals quickly.
items.exampleCN: 会算数的读者能很快核对总数。

items.meaning: the number above the line in a fraction
items.example: In three quarters, three is the numerator.
items.exampleCN: 在四分之三里，三是分子。

items.meaning: to list items one by one
items.example: The report enumerates every source of error.
items.exampleCN: 报告逐项列出了每一种误差来源。

items.example: Numerous studies report the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 众多研究报告了同样的模式。

items.example: The storm left innumerable branches on the road.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨在路面上留下数不清的树枝。

definition_zh: 大量存在；充满；富于；盛产
definition_en: to exist in large numbers or quantities, or to be full of something
core_image: 水从容器边缘漫出来，四周到处都是
scene: 雨后的草坡上，蘑菇一丛丛冒出来。 Mushrooms abound on the wet hillside after rain.
sceneCN: 这里 abound 是「大量存在」（第 1 个义项：某物数量很多地出现）；句意为雨后湿润的山坡上蘑菇大量生长。

pos.zh: 大量存在；众多
富于；充满

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「丰富；充裕」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「丰富的；大量的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「丰富地；大量地」

senses.title: To exist in large numbers
senses.definition: of things, to be present in large numbers or quantities
senses.definitionCN: 指事物以很大的数量出现
senses.example: Wild flowers abound in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷里野花繁盛。
senses.why: Latin abundare meant 'to overflow'; what abounds is so plentiful that it spills over the edges of the container.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abundare 意为「溢出」；abound 的东西多到从容器边缘漫出来。

senses.title: To be rich in something
senses.definition: to have a great deal of a particular quality or thing
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量的某种性质或事物
senses.example: The region abounds in mineral resources.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区矿产资源丰富。
senses.why: A place that overflows with a resource is described with in or with, the container and its contents named together.
senses.whyCN: 一个充满某种资源的地方用 in 或 with 来连接，容器与内容被一起说出。

senses.title: Of animals: to be numerous
senses.definition: of animals or plants, to occur in great numbers in a habitat
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物在某一栖息地大量出现
senses.example: Deer abound in these forests.
senses.exampleCN: 这些森林里鹿群众多。
senses.why: Living things that fill a habitat are pictured as filling a vessel to overflowing.
senses.whyCN: 填满栖息地的生物，被想象成把容器装到溢出。

senses.title: Of talk or rumour: to circulate widely
senses.definition: of stories, rumours, or ideas, to be widespread
senses.definitionCN: 指说法、传闻或观念广泛流传
senses.example: Rumours abound about the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 关于合并的传闻四起。
senses.why: Words and stories can also overflow a community, spreading faster than anyone can count.
senses.whyCN: 话语与故事也会漫过一个社群，传播得比谁数得都快。

senses.title: Of a place: to produce plentifully
senses.definition: of a region or farm, to yield large crops or products
senses.definitionCN: 指地区或农场产出大量作物或产品
senses.example: The orchards abound with apples in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天果园里苹果累累。
senses.why: The overflow image turns agricultural: the harvest is more than the baskets can hold.
senses.whyCN: 溢出的意象转向农业：收成多到篮子装不下。

senses.title: To be filled with problems
senses.definition: to be full of something undesirable, such as errors or complaints
senses.definitionCN: 充满不想要的东西，如错误或抱怨
senses.example: The report abounds with errors.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告错误百出。
senses.why: The same 'full to overflowing' pattern works for defects, which crowd a text as water crowds a jar.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「满到溢出」结构也适用于缺陷，它们挤满文本，像水挤满罐子。

senses.title: Of resources: to be plentiful
senses.definition: of resources or supplies, to be available in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 指资源或供给以大量形式存在
senses.example: Clean water abounds in the northern valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 北部山谷中清洁水源充裕。
senses.why: Plenty is measured as volume: a resource that abounds is one whose supply spills past demand.
senses.whyCN: 充裕以体量来衡量：abound 的资源就是供给溢过需求。

senses.title: Of ideas: to spring up
senses.definition: of ideas or possibilities, to appear in great number
senses.definitionCN: 指想法或可能性大量出现
senses.example: New ideas abound at the start of a project.
senses.exampleCN: 项目开始时新想法层出不穷。
senses.why: Abstract things are imagined as a flow that rises and spreads, so an active period is one where ideas abound.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物被想象成上涨漫开的流，因此活跃时期就是想法 abound 的时期。

intro.en: Abound comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to overflow', built from a prefix and the word for a wave.
intro.cn: abound 来自一个意为「溢出」的拉丁语动词，由前缀与表示「波浪」的词构成。

items.en: The root *wed- is reconstructed with the sense 'water'; it also lies behind English water and wet.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *wed- 被重构为「水」之义；英语 water 与 wet 也源自它。

items.en: unda meant 'a wave, water', and it produced undulate and inundate.
items.cn: unda 意为「波浪、水」，衍生出 undulate 与 inundate。

items.en: undare meant 'to rise in waves, flow', a verb of water moving in volume.
items.cn: undare 意为「波浪涌起、流动」，是一个表示水大量运动的动词。

items.en: ab- 'away, from' plus undare formed abundare, 'to overflow, be plentiful'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 undare 构成 abundare，意为「溢出、丰盛」。

items.en: Old French abonder carried the sense 'to be plentiful' into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 abonder 把「丰盛」之义带入中世纪用法。

items.en: English abound keeps the two patterns abound in and abound with, and extends to rumours, errors, and ideas.
items.cn: 英语 abound 保留 abound in 与 abound with 两种结构，并扩展到传闻、错误与想法。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adjective, and adverb from the same family, plus two water-root words; the second gathers verbs for being plentiful.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名词、形容词与副词，以及两个同「水」词根的词；第二组收表示丰盛的动词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning a very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丰富、充裕」，指某物数量极大。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning existing in large quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「丰富的、大量的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'plentifully or very clearly'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「丰富地、大量地」，也可表示「十分清楚地」。

entries.definition: To flood or overwhelm, from the Latin word for a wave.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「淹没、使应接不暇」，来自表示波浪的拉丁词。

entries.definition: To move in waves, from the same Latin noun unda.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动、起伏」，来自同一个拉丁名词 unda。

entries.definition: To be full of things, especially living things, moving in great numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「充满、涌动」，尤指大量生物活动。

entries.definition: To move or gather in large numbers, like bees.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「成群移动、蜂拥」，像蜜蜂一样大量聚集。

entries.definition: To increase rapidly in number.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激增、迅速繁殖」。

entries.definition: To grow or develop well and plentifully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「繁茂、兴旺」，生长或发展得很好很多。

entries.definition: To be so full that contents spill over.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「溢出」，满到内容物漫出。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two fixed patterns abound in and abound with and the water image; the abstract hooks picture the overflow.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 abund in 与 abound with 两个固定结构及水的意象；抽象记忆点想象溢出。

normal.en: Abound in and abound with are the two patterns; in names the place, with names the contents.
normal.cn: abound in 与 abound with 是两个结构；in 引出地点，with 引出内容。

normal.en: Abundance is the noun and abundant the adjective, both from the same overflow image.
normal.cn: 名词是 abundance，形容词是 abundant，二者都来自同一个「溢出」意象。

normal.en: Rumours abound and opportunities abound are common news and business phrases.
normal.cn: rumours abound 与 opportunities abound 是常见新闻与商业短语。

normal.en: The Latin source is undare, 'to flow in waves', so abound is water overflowing a rim.
normal.cn: 拉丁来源是 undare（波浪流动），因此 abound 就是水漫过边缘。

normal.en: The -s form abounds is used with singular subjects such as wildlife.
normal.cn: -s 形式 abounds 与 wildlife 等单数主语连用。

abstract.en: Picture a barrel filled until water runs down its sides.
abstract.cn: 想象木桶被装到水从桶壁流下。

abstract.en: Picture mushrooms pushing up through wet grass in every direction.
abstract.cn: 想象蘑菇从湿润的草丛里向四面八方冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a room so full of talking people that voices spill into the street.
abstract.cn: 想象房间挤满说话的人，声音漫到街上。

examples.en: Fish abound in these cold rivers.
examples.cn: 这些寒冷的河流里鱼群繁多。

examples.en: The internet abounds with misleading claims.
examples.cn: 网络上充斥着误导性说法。

examples.en: Examples of this pattern abound in the corpus.
examples.cn: 这种模式的例子在语料库中大量存在。

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from 'overflow': things, animals, words, crops, resources, and ideas can all fill a space past its edges.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都从「溢出」生长出来：事物、动物、言语、作物、资源与想法，都能把空间装到漫出边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water running over the rim of a full vessel
core.cn: 核心意象：水从装满的容器边缘漫出

branches.en: Things, animals, and crops fill a place beyond counting.
branches.cn: 事物、动物与作物把一处空间装到数不清。

branches.en: A place or supply is rich in a resource, named with in or with.
branches.cn: 某地或供给富于某种资源，用 in 或 with 引出。

branches.en: Words and rumours fill a community and spread widely.
branches.cn: 言语与传闻充满社群并广泛传播。

branches.en: Undesirable things such as errors crowd a text.
branches.cn: 错误等不想要的东西挤满文本。

branches.en: Ideas rise and spread in an active period.
branches.cn: 在活跃时期，想法涌起并扩散。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem abund-, the noun ending -ance, and the adjective and adverb endings -ant and -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 abund-、名词后缀 -ance，以及形容词与副词后缀 -ant、-ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abundare and unda are the direct source of abound and its family, so the Latin entries record both the verb and the wave noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abundare 与 unda 是 abound 及其词族的直接来源，因此拉丁条目同时记录动词与「波浪」名词。

definition_zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严苛的；严酷的
definition_en: carried out with great care and strict standards, leaving no step unchecked
core_image: 实验室里每份样本都要两个人各自核对，记录上少一行就整批重做
scene: 实验室里，每一批样本都要两人分别核对，任何一步记录不全就得重做。 The trial's rigorous protocol required two independent checks for every sample.
sceneCN: 这里指标准严格、不留缺口（第 1 个义项：严格而彻底的）；句意为该试验的严谨规程要求每份样本都做两次独立核对。图中可辨识物件：样本架、双人核对表、签名栏、重做标记。

pos.zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严酷的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「严格地；严谨地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「严格；严谨」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「严格；严酷；严谨」
由同一拉丁动词的另一形容词形式构成，义为「坚硬的；僵化的」
由「僵硬的」加名词尾构成，义为「刚性；僵化」

senses.title: Strict and thorough
senses.definition: done with great care and with no step left unchecked
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的仔细进行，每一步都被核查
senses.example: The safety review was rigorous, and nothing was signed off on trust.
senses.exampleCN: 安全审查十分严格，没有任何一项是靠信任签字的。
senses.why: The Latin root means stiffness, and a stiff procedure does not bend to convenience.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「僵硬」，僵硬的程序不会为图方便而弯折。

senses.title: Demanding testing
senses.definition: testing carried out under hard, controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在严苛且有控制的条件下进行的测试
senses.example: The battery underwent rigorous testing at high and low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 电池在高温与低温下接受了严苛测试。
senses.why: Tests are rigorous when the conditions are harder than ordinary use.
senses.whyCN: 当条件比日常使用更苛刻，测试就是严苛的。

senses.title: A proof with no gaps
senses.definition: a proof in which every step is justified
senses.definitionCN: 每一步都有依据的证明
senses.example: A rigorous proof does not rely on a diagram that merely looks right.
senses.exampleCN: 严密的证明不依赖一张只是看起来正确的图。
senses.why: In mathematics the word means the argument cannot be loosened anywhere.
senses.whyCN: 在数学里，这个词意味着论证在任何一处都不能放松。

senses.title: Hard training
senses.definition: training that is physically or mentally severe
senses.definitionCN: 在体力或心力上都很艰苦的训练
senses.example: Rigorous training prepared the crew for a month at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 严酷的训练让船员为海上一个月做好了准备。
senses.why: Training borrows the word because a strict method also trains the will.
senses.whyCN: 训练借用这个词，因为严格的方法也在训练意志。

senses.title: Standards without shortcuts
senses.definition: standards that admit no exceptions for convenience
senses.definitionCN: 不为方便开例外口子的标准
senses.example: The journal applies rigorous standards to every submission, even invited ones.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊对每篇投稿都适用严格标准，受邀稿也不例外。
senses.why: A standard is rigorous when the exception costs more than the rule.
senses.whyCN: 当例外的代价高于规则，标准才是严格的。

senses.title: Analysis that checks its assumptions
senses.definition: analysis that tests its own assumptions rather than assuming them
senses.definitionCN: 检验自身假设、而不是直接假定成立的分析
senses.example: A rigorous analysis of the survey must first ask who was not asked.
senses.exampleCN: 对这项调查的严谨分析，首先要问谁没有被问到。
senses.why: The analysis turns the strictness on itself, which is the highest form of the method.
senses.whyCN: 分析把严格对准自身，这是该方法最高的形态。

senses.title: Selection by hard tests
senses.definition: choosing only those who pass demanding tests
senses.definitionCN: 只让通过高要求测试者入选
senses.example: The fellowship uses a rigorous selection process with three rounds of review.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金采用三轮评审的严格筛选流程。
senses.why: Selection is rigorous when the gate, not the label, does the choosing.
senses.whyCN: 当做出选择的是门槛而不是标签，筛选才是严格的。

senses.title: Enforcement without leniency
senses.definition: applying a rule fully, with no relaxed exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 完整执行规则，不作宽松的例外
senses.example: Rigorous enforcement of the smoking ban changed behaviour within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 禁烟规定的严格执行在一个月内改变了行为。
senses.why: Enforcement completes the word: the rule now has hands as well as words.
senses.whyCN: 执行补全了这个词：规则如今不光有条文，还有手。

intro.en: Rigorous comes from Latin rigor, stiffness or hardness, from rigere, to be stiff, with an adjective ending that reached English through French. The physical stiffness became a moral and methodological one: a standard that will not bend. The same root also gives rigid and rigor mortis.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 rigor「僵硬、坚硬」，出自 rigere「僵直」，加形容词尾后经法语进入英语。身体上的僵硬变成了道德与方法的僵硬：不肯弯折的标准。同一词根还给出 rigid 与「尸僵」一语。

items.en: Rigere meant to be stiff or numb, said of limbs and of cold.
items.cn: 这个词意为僵直、麻木，用于肢体，也用于寒冷。

items.en: Rigor named stiffness, hardness and, by extension, severity of rule or climate.
items.cn: 这个词指僵硬、坚硬，并引申指规则或气候的严酷。

items.en: Later Latin formed an adjective meaning full of stiffness or severity.
items.cn: 后起拉丁语构成形容词，意为「充满僵硬或严酷的」。

items.en: French carried the adjective into the language of law and method.
items.cn: 法语把该形容词带入法律与方法的语言。

items.en: English applied it to rules, proofs and training.
items.cn: 英语把它用于规则、证明与训练。

items.en: Research methods fixed phrases such as rigorous testing; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 科研方法固定了「严苛测试」等说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the stiffness root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of strictness. The note warns that vigorous looks like a relative but comes from a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「僵硬」词根或形近；第二组指其他「严格」的说法。这里提醒：形近的「精力充沛」一词出自另一词根，并非同族。

entries.definition: Strictness or severity, and in medicine, a chill.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格或严酷，医学上指寒战。

entries.definition: Stiff and unable to bend, literally or in attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 指僵硬不能弯，字面或态度上皆可。

entries.definition: In a strict and thorough way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以严格而彻底的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being strict and thorough.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格而彻底的性质。

entries.definition: Full of energy and strength; its root means to be lively, not stiff.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、强健；其词根意为「有生气」，并非「僵硬」。

entries.definition: Insisting on exact obedience to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚持对规则的精确遵守。

entries.definition: Complete, with no part left out.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整、没有遗漏任何部分。

entries.definition: Showing extreme attention to small details.
entries.definitionCN: 指对细小处极度注意。

entries.definition: Tight and demanding, often of rules or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧而苛刻，多用于规则或条件。

entries.definition: Demanding a great deal of effort or precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求大量努力或精确。

entries.definition: Harsh in force or treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指在力度或对待上严厉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two signature lines, the frozen joint, the long proof and the three-round review.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两行签名、冻僵的关节、冗长的证明与三轮评审。

normal.en: A rigorous process has two signatures where one would do.
normal.cn: 严谨的流程在一个签名够用的地方放两个。

normal.en: Rigid means the joint will not bend; rigorous means the rule will not bend.
normal.cn: 「僵硬的」说关节不弯，「严格的」说规则不弯。

normal.en: A rigorous proof leaves no step to the reader's goodwill.
normal.cn: 严密的证明不把任何一步留给读者的善意。

normal.en: Rigorous training is remembered in the body, not in the notes.
normal.cn: 严酷的训练被记在身体里，而不是记在笔记里。

normal.en: Vigorous is about energy and rigorous is about stiffness, though they sound alike.
normal.cn: 「强健的」讲精力，「严格的」讲僵硬，尽管读音相似。

abstract.en: Strictness is a promise that the result will not depend on who was watching.
abstract.cn: 严格是一种承诺：结果不取决于当时谁在看。

abstract.en: The same stiffness that protects a result can freeze a field for a generation.
abstract.cn: 保护结果的那种僵硬，也可能把一个领域冻住一代人。

abstract.en: A rigorous standard is expensive, which is why it is often replaced by its description.
abstract.cn: 严格的标准很贵，所以常被它的描述所取代。

examples.en: The claim survived rigorous testing by three independent laboratories.
examples.cn: 这一主张经受了三家独立实验室的严苛测试。

examples.en: Her analysis was rigorous, and it questioned the survey's own assumptions.
examples.cn: 她的分析很严谨，也质疑了调查自身的假设。

examples.en: Rigorous enforcement, not new rules, reduced the accident rate.
examples.cn: 降低事故率的是严格执行，而不是新规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞格若斯」：规矩「硬」得像冻住的关节，一步也不肯弯，检查才做得严

root: 源于拉丁语表示「僵直」的动词，其名词义为「僵硬、严酷」，后起形容词再经法语进入英语。同族有表示「严格」「僵硬的」「刚性」的词；形近而表示「精力充沛」的词出自表示「有生气」的另一词根。十六世纪进入英语；各技术短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn stiffness into method: a thorough procedure, demanding tests, gapless proofs, hard training, standards without shortcuts, self-checking analysis, strict selection, and full enforcement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「僵硬」变成方法：彻底的流程、严苛的测试、无缺口的证明、艰苦的训练、不许走捷径的标准、自查假设的分析、严格筛选与完整执行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signatures on every sheet, and a whole batch is redone if one line is missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：每张记录上两个签名，少一行就整批重做。

branches.en: THE STIFF PROCEDURE: care that refuses convenience in every ordinary step.
branches.cn: 僵硬的程序：在每个寻常步骤上都不为方便让步。

branches.en: THE HARD TEST AND THE HARD DRILL: strict conditions, and training built under them.
branches.cn: 严苛的测试与艰苦的训练：严格的条件，以及在条件下筑起的训练。

branches.en: THE CLOSED ARGUMENT: proofs and analyses with no step left to goodwill.
branches.cn: 封闭的论证：不把任何一步留给善意的证明与分析。

branches.en: THE UNBENDING RULE: standards and enforcement that admit no exceptions.
branches.cn: 不肯弯的规则：不容例外开的标准与执行。

branches.en: THE NARROW GATE: selection that only lets the tested through.
branches.cn: 窄门：只让过关者进入的筛选。

intro.en: Rigorous is a Latin stiffness noun with an adjective ending; its family covers rigidity, strictness and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「僵硬」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖刚性、严格与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rigere and rigor supply the stiffness, and the later adjective rigorosus gives the English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「僵直」与「僵硬」提供词干，后起形容词给出英语形态。

items.example: The oldest root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族最古老的根。

items.example: It gives English rigor.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语的「严格」。

items.example: It gives the English adjective its shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语形容词的形态。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把该词标为形容词。

items.example: It forms rigorously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「严格地」。

items.example: It forms rigorousness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「严谨」。

items.example: A same-root word from a different form.
items.exampleCN: 同词根但由另一形式构成的词。

items.example: Built on rigid, not on rigorous.
items.exampleCN: 由「僵硬的」构成，而非由本词构成。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「严格地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「严谨」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「严格；严酷」
由同一拉丁动词的另一形容词形式构成，义为「僵硬的」

definition_zh: 气候重建；依据代用资料复原过去气候的工作及其结果
definition_en: the work of rebuilding the climate of a past period from proxy evidence, or the series produced by that work
core_image: 长桌上摊着年轮切片、冰芯管与珊瑚薄片，一只手把散落的点连成一条起伏的曲线
scene: 实验室的长桌上摊着年轮切片、冰芯管与珊瑚薄片，研究员把散落的点连成一条曲线。 A climate reconstruction turns scattered proxies into one long temperature curve.
sceneCN: 这里指把零散证据复原成过去气候的工作（第 1 个义项：重建工作）；句意为一次气候重建把分散的代用资料接成一条长长的温度曲线。图中可辨识物件：年轮切片、冰芯管、珊瑚薄片、坐标纸。

pos.zh: 气候重建；复原过去气候的工作与结果

derivatives.zh: 由表示「再次」的前缀加「建造」的动词构成，义为「重建；复原」
由重建动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「重建；重建物」
由重建动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「重建的；复原性的」
由同一希腊词干经拉丁语而来，义为「气候」
指代替直接测量使用的代用资料，是重建工作的证据来源

senses.title: The work of rebuilding a past climate
senses.definition: the research process of assembling evidence and methods to recover the climate of a past period
senses.definitionCN: 汇集证据与方法以复原某一过去时期气候的研究过程
senses.example: The climate reconstruction took five years and three field seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这次气候重建花了五年和三个野外季节。
senses.why: The noun names the activity first, because the phrase literally describes building again something that no longer exists.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词首先指活动，因为该短语字面上就是把已经不存在的东西再次建造起来。

senses.title: The resulting series
senses.definition: the ordered sequence of past temperatures or rainfall values produced by the work
senses.definitionCN: 由重建工作产出的过去温度或降水数值的有序序列
senses.example: The published climate reconstruction runs from the tenth century to the present.
senses.exampleCN: 发表的那条气候重建序列从十世纪一直延续到今天。
senses.why: A finished reconstruction is a line of numbers through time, so the same noun names the output.
senses.whyCN: 完成的重建是一条贯穿时间的数字曲线，因此同一个名词也指成果。

senses.title: A proxy-based method
senses.definition: a technique that converts tree rings, ice, corals or sediments into climate information
senses.definitionCN: 把树木年轮、冰、珊瑚或沉积物转成气候信息的技术
senses.example: The team used a climate reconstruction built on tree rings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队采用了一种建立在树木年轮上的气候重建。
senses.why: Since no thermometer reaches the past, the phrase often labels the method that substitutes natural archives for instruments.
senses.whyCN: 没有温度计能抵达过去，因此这个短语常指用自然档案替代仪器的方法。

senses.title: A regional reconstruction
senses.definition: a reconstruction limited to one region, such as a basin, a coast or a plateau
senses.definitionCN: 限于一个区域的重建，如某个盆地、海岸或高原
senses.example: Their regional climate reconstruction covers the whole Mediterranean basin.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的区域气候重建覆盖整个地中海盆地。
senses.why: Evidence is local, so the phrase is routinely narrowed to a named area before it is widened.
senses.whyCN: 证据是局地的，所以这个短语常先收窄到某个具体地区，再向外推广。

senses.title: A global reconstruction
senses.definition: a reconstruction that merges records from many regions into a single world-wide picture
senses.definitionCN: 把许多地区的记录并成一幅全球图景的重建
senses.example: A global climate reconstruction combines records from every continent.
senses.exampleCN: 一次全球气候重建把各大洲的记录合并起来。
senses.why: One region cannot answer a planetary question, so the phrase scales up to the whole globe.
senses.whyCN: 一个区域回答不了行星尺度的问题，于是这个短语扩展到整个地球。

senses.title: A year-by-year reconstruction
senses.definition: a reconstruction fine enough to give one value for each year or each season
senses.definitionCN: 精细到每年或每季给出一个数值的重建
senses.example: The annual climate reconstruction resolves every single year.
senses.exampleCN: 这条年度气候重建能分辨每一年。
senses.why: Resolution is the quality that matters most, so the phrase is modified by the time step it can resolve.
senses.whyCN: 分辨率是最要紧的品质，因此这个短语常受它能分辨的时间步长修饰。

senses.title: One member of an ensemble
senses.definition: a single reconstruction among several that differ in proxies, methods or assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 在代用资料、方法或假设上有所不同的若干重建中的一套
senses.example: Each climate reconstruction in the set uses slightly different proxies.
senses.exampleCN: 这一组里的每一套气候重建都使用了略有差异的代用资料。
senses.why: Science rarely trusts one curve, so the phrase is counted and compared as one member of a family.
senses.whyCN: 科学很少只信一条曲线，因此这个短语会被当作一族中的一员来计数与比较。

senses.title: A reconstruction used to test models
senses.definition: a past-climate series employed as a target against which climate simulations are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用作目标、用来评判气候模拟结果的过去气候序列
senses.example: The model was checked against a climate reconstruction of the last millennium.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型对照过去一千年的气候重建接受了检验。
senses.why: A simulation needs an independent past to beat or match, and the phrase supplies the yardstick.
senses.whyCN: 模拟需要一个独立的过去来比较，这个短语就提供了那把尺子。

intro.en: The phrase joins climate, from Greek klima through Latin clima, to reconstruction, from Latin struere, to pile up, through construere, to build, plus re-, again, and -ion, a noun ending. The whole phrase is a twentieth-century formation; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「climate」与「reconstruction」接在一起：前者从希腊语「klima」经拉丁语「clima」而来；后者来自拉丁语「struere」「堆起」，经「construere」「建造」，再加表示「再次」的前缀与名词词尾。整短语是二十世纪构造，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Klima named a slope or a zone of the earth, since the sun's angle was thought to shape each region.
items.cn: 这个词指斜坡或地表的地带，因为太阳角度被认为塑造了每个区域。

items.en: Latin clima kept the zone sense, and English climate slowly narrowed to the weather of a region.
items.cn: 拉丁语「clima」保留了地带之意，英语「climate」则慢慢收窄为某一地区的天气。

items.en: Struere meant to pile up or arrange, the plain act of stacking material into a structure.
items.cn: 这个词意为堆起、排列，即把材料堆成结构的朴素动作。

items.en: Construere added the idea of bringing pieces together, and English construct came from it.
items.cn: 这个词加上了把各件东西聚拢的意思，英语的「construct」由此而来。

items.en: The prefix re- means again and the ending -ion makes a noun of action or result, giving reconstruction.
items.cn: 前缀表示「再次」，词尾把动作或结果变成名词，于是有了「reconstruction」。

items.en: The full phrase climate reconstruction belongs to the twentieth century; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 完整的短语「climate reconstruction」属于二十世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like climate reconstruction; the second group names neighbouring ideas of past-climate evidence and model testing.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「climate reconstruction」相近；第二组是与「过去气候证据、模型检验」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act or result of building something again, the noun inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指再次建造的动作或结果，是短语内部的名词。

entries.definition: To build again from evidence, the verb behind the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指依据证据重新构建，是短语背后的动词。

entries.definition: Serving to rebuild, often used of surgery or of historical work.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于重建的，常用于外科手术或历史工作。

entries.definition: The act of building, without the idea of doing it a second time.
entries.definitionCN: 指建造的动作，但不含「再一次」的意思。

entries.definition: The long-term weather of a region, the first half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地区的长期天气，是短语的前一半。

entries.definition: A natural archive that stands in for direct climate measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指代替直接气候测量的自然档案。

entries.definition: The ancient climate itself, which a reconstruction aims to recover.
entries.definitionCN: 指古代气候本身，正是重建工作要复原的对象。

entries.definition: The sequence of past climates, close to the result sense of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指过去气候的序列，接近这个短语的结果义。

entries.definition: A model run aimed at a past period, the operation that consumes a reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对过去时段运行模型，正是使用重建结果的操作。

entries.definition: A reconstruction of recent climate built by combining observations with models.
entries.definitionCN: 指把观测与模型结合、重建近代气候的产品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the literal pieces of the phrase, its real evidence and its real modelling use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个短语的字面成分、真实证据与真实建模用途。

normal.en: Climate plus reconstruction: you build the weather of the past a second time from what it left behind.
normal.cn: 气候加重建：用过去留下的东西，把当年的天气再建一次。

normal.en: The Latin struere meant to pile up, which is exactly what a reconstruction does with dated points.
normal.cn: 拉丁语的「struere」意为堆起，而重建正是把有年代的散点堆叠起来。

normal.en: A climate reconstruction is usually built from tree rings, ice cores, corals and lake mud.
normal.cn: 气候重建通常由树木年轮、冰芯、珊瑚与湖泥搭成。

normal.en: High-resolution climate reconstruction is the phrase used when every year can be told apart.
normal.cn: 当每一年都能分辨时，用的说法就是高分辨率气候重建。

normal.en: A reconstruction of the last millennium is the standard target for testing climate models.
normal.cn: 过去一千年的重建是检验气候模型的标准靶子。

abstract.en: A reconstruction is a bridge built from both ends: evidence from the past, questions from the present.
abstract.cn: 重建是一座从两端搭起的桥：一端是过去的证据，一端是现在的问题。

abstract.en: The past left no thermometer, only scraps; reconstruction is the act of reading a line into those scraps.
abstract.cn: 过去没有留下温度计，只留下碎片；重建就是把这些碎片读成一条线。

abstract.en: Each curve is a second building of something that can never be visited again.
abstract.cn: 每条曲线都是对一座再也无法到访的建筑的二次建造。

examples.en: The climate reconstruction relies on corals from the tropical Pacific.
examples.cn: 这次气候重建依靠热带太平洋的珊瑚。

examples.en: They compared every climate reconstruction available for the last two thousand years.
examples.cn: 他们比较了过去两千年所有可用的气候重建。

examples.en: A good climate reconstruction must state its uncertainty clearly.
examples.cn: 一份好的气候重建必须清楚说明自身的不确定性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「克莱美特 瑞肯斯特拉克申」——气候被拆成零件，再按年代重新搭回去：气候重建。

root: 「climate」源于希腊语「klima」「倾斜、地带」，经拉丁语「clima」进入英语；「reconstruction」来自拉丁语「struere」「堆起、建造」，经「construere」「堆在一起、建造」得「construct」，再加表示「再次」的前缀与名词词尾；整短语属二十世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the work itself to its output, its proxy method, a region, the globe, a yearly resolution, one member of an ensemble, and a yardstick for models.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从重建工作本身走向它的成果、代用资料方法、一个区域、全球、逐年分辨率、多套中的一套，以及检验模型的尺子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered dated points on a long table are joined into one temperature curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌上散落的有年代的点，被接成一条温度曲线。

branches.en: THE WORK: hands and methods assemble evidence until a past climate can be stated.
branches.cn: 重建工作：双手与方法汇集证据，直到过去的气候可以被陈述。

branches.en: THE CURVE AND THE METHOD: the finished series, and the proxy technique that produced it.
branches.cn: 曲线与方法：完成的序列，以及产出它的代用资料技术。

branches.en: THE LOCAL AND THE PLANETARY: one basin filled in, then every continent joined together.
branches.cn: 局地与行星：先填满一个盆地，再把各大洲接成整体。

branches.en: THE FINE AND THE MANY: a year-by-year line, and one member among several competing lines.
branches.cn: 精细与多套：逐年的曲线，以及若干竞争曲线中的一套。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: the reconstructed past becomes the target a simulation must match.
branches.cn: 尺子：被重建的过去成为模拟必须对上的目标。

intro.en: Climate reconstruction joins a Greek-derived climate word to a Latin-derived building word and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的「气候」词、拉丁来源的「建造」词与一个名词词尾接在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies clima for climate, struere and construere for building, and the prefix and ending that make reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示气候的「clima」、表示建造的「struere」与「construere」，以及构成「重建」的前缀与词尾。

items.example: The zone word became the climate word.
items.exampleCN: 这个地带词后来变成了气候词。

items.example: Latin carried the word into English usage.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词带进了英语的用法。

items.example: It is the first half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个短语的前一半。

items.example: The verb names the act of stacking material.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把材料堆叠起来的动作。

items.example: English construct descends from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语的「construct」源自这个动词。

items.example: It marks the second building of the same thing.
items.exampleCN: 它标出对同一事物的第二次建造。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun.

items.exampleCN: 较短的动词包含在较长的名词里。

definition_zh: 不成功的；夭折的；中途失败的；发育不全的
definition_en: failing to achieve its purpose, or coming to an end before completion
core_image: 刚点火的火箭在半空断成两截，落回地面
scene: 队伍在山口折返，暴风雪让这次突袭彻底落空。 The abortive raid ended before the troops reached the pass.
sceneCN: 这里 abortive 是「中途失败的」（第 1 个义项：行动未达目的便告终止）；句意为这次突袭在部队抵达山口前就失败了。

pos.zh: 失败的；夭折的
（医学）顿挫的；（生物学）发育不全的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「中止；流产」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「流产；中止」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「失败地；中途终止地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「失败性；夭折状态」

senses.title: Failing to reach its aim
senses.definition: of an action or attempt, ending in failure before its goal is reached
senses.definitionCN: 指行动或尝试在达到目标之前以失败告终
senses.example: The rescue was an abortive attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援是一次失败的尝试。
senses.why: Latin aboriri meant 'to miscarry', from ab- 'away' and oriri 'to be born'; an abortive action is one whose outcome never comes to birth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aboriri 意为「流产」，由 ab-（离开）与 oriri（出生）构成；abortive 的行动就是结果从未「出生」的行动。

senses.title: Of a plan that collapses
senses.definition: of a plan or scheme, failing before it can be carried out
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或方案在付诸实施前就失败
senses.example: Their abortive plan cost the company a fortune.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夭折的计划让公司损失了一大笔钱。
senses.why: A plan is expected to be 'born' in action; if it collapses early, it is abortive in the same obstetrical image.
senses.whyCN: 计划本应在行动中「诞生」；若早早崩解，就同样落入这个产科意象，成为 abortive。

senses.title: Of a revolt that fails
senses.definition: describing a uprising or coup that is put down or collapses
senses.definitionCN: 形容被镇压或自行瓦解的起义或政变
senses.example: The abortive uprising lasted only two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败的起义只持续了两天。
senses.why: A revolt is an attempted birth of a new order; crushed before it takes hold, it earns the word.
senses.whyCN: 起义是试图让新秩序「诞生」；在站稳之前被压碎，就得到这个词。

senses.title: Of medical treatment
senses.definition: describing treatment that stops a disease in its early stage
senses.definitionCN: 形容在疾病早期将其截断的治疗
senses.example: Doctors used abortive treatment to shorten the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用顿挫疗法缩短病程。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the 'cut short' sense literally: the treatment aborts the disease's course.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了字面的「截断」义：这种治疗把疾病的进程截断。

senses.title: Of an organ that never develops
senses.definition: of a body part, remaining small and non-functional
senses.definitionCN: 指身体部位保持很小且无功能
senses.example: The whale retains an abortive hind limb.
senses.exampleCN: 鲸保留着一条发育不全的后肢。
senses.why: Biology borrows the image of a process that stops before completion: the organ's growth is aborted.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了「过程未完成便停止」的意象：这个器官的生长被中止了。

senses.title: Of a pregnancy that ends early
senses.definition: describing a pregnancy or birth process that ends before it can continue
senses.definitionCN: 形容在继续之前就终止的妊娠或生产进程
senses.example: The term abortive is used for therapies that prevent a pregnancy from continuing.
senses.exampleCN: abortive 一词用于阻止妊娠继续的疗法。
senses.why: This is the literal source of the word: a process that should have led to birth stops on the way.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最字面的来源：本应导向出生的过程在中途停下。

senses.title: Of an effort that comes to nothing
senses.definition: of work or effort, producing no lasting result
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或努力没有产生持久结果
senses.example: All their abortive efforts left the bridge unbuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 他们所有徒劳的努力都没能让桥建成。
senses.why: Effort is expected to give birth to a result; when nothing is delivered, the effort is abortive.
senses.whyCN: 努力本应「生出」结果；当什么也没产出时，这份努力就是 abortive。

senses.title: Of a movement that stops short
senses.titleCN: 中途停止的运动或进程
senses.definition: of a process or movement, halting before its natural end
senses.definitionCN: 指进程或运动在自然结束前停下
senses.example: The reform was an abortive move that changed nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革是一次中途停止、什么也没改变的举动。
senses.why: The general sense is simply 'cut off before completion', the widest extension of the original image.
senses.whyCN: 最一般的义项就是「在完成前被截断」，这是原初意象最宽的延伸。

intro.en: Abortive comes from the Latin verb for miscarrying, whose parts mean 'away' and 'to be born'.
intro.cn: abortive 来自表示「流产」的拉丁语动词，其成分意为「离开」与「出生」。

items.en: oriri meant 'to rise, appear, be born'; it also produced origin and orient.
items.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出现、出生」，也衍生出 origin 与 orient。

items.en: ab is the preposition 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: aboriri meant 'to miscarry, fail to be born', built from ab- and oriri.
items.cn: aboriri 意为「流产、未能出生」，由 ab- 与 oriri 构成。

items.en: The past participle abortus gave the noun for a miscarriage and the adjective abortivus.
items.cn: 过去分词 abortus 构成表示流产的名词，并衍生出形容词 abortivus。

items.en: English adopted abortive first in the medical sense and then for any failed enterprise.
items.cn: 英语先吸收 abortive 的医学义，随后用于任何失败的事业。

items.en: Modern usage applies the word to plans, revolts, efforts, and underdeveloped organs.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词用于计划、起义、努力与发育不全的器官。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, noun, and adverb from the same family; the second gathers adjectives for failure and futility.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的动词、名词与副词；第二组收表示失败与徒劳的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stop a process before it finishes.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「中止、流产」，指在完成前停止某个过程。

entries.definition: The noun for the ending of a pregnancy or the failure of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流产；中止」，指妊娠终止或进程失败。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a failed or cut-short way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「失败地、中途终止地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being abortive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失败性、夭折状态」。

entries.definition: Not achieving the intended result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不成功的」，未达到预期结果。

entries.definition: Useless because it cannot produce a result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「徒劳的」，因无法产生结果而无用。

entries.definition: Producing no useful outcome, like a tree with no fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无成果的」，像不结果的树一样没有有用产出。

entries.definition: Having not succeeded in what was attempted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失败的」，在尝试的事情上没有成功。

entries.definition: Producing no result despite effort.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「徒然的」，尽管努力却没有结果。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the obstetrical image behind the word and the standard collocations; the abstract hooks picture a process cut off midway.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用词后的产科意象与标准搭配；抽象记忆点想象中途被截断的过程。

normal.en: Abortive and abort share the Latin image of a birth that does not happen.
normal.cn: abortive 与 abort 共享「未能出生的生产」这一拉丁意象。

normal.en: An abortive attempt, an abortive coup, and an abortive plan are standard collocations.
normal.cn: an abortive attempt、an abortive coup、an abortive plan 都是标准搭配。

normal.en: Abortive treatment is a medical phrase for stopping a disease early.
normal.cn: abortive treatment 是医学术语，指早期截断疾病。

normal.en: Abortive organ describes a body part that never fully develops.
normal.cn: abortive organ 指从未完全发育的身体部位。

normal.en: The -ive ending turns the action into a quality: what fails is abortive.
normal.cn: -ive 结尾把动作变成性质：失败的东西就是 abortive。

abstract.en: Picture a rocket that breaks apart in mid-air and falls back to the pad.
abstract.cn: 想象火箭在半空断成两截，落回发射台。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge half built, then abandoned with its arches open to the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一座建到一半就被放弃的桥，拱架空对天空。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that sprouts, then withers before the first leaf opens.
abstract.cn: 想象种子发了芽，却在第一片叶子展开前枯萎。

examples.en: The attack was abortive and the troops withdrew.
examples.cn: 进攻失败，部队撤退了。

examples.en: They made an abortive attempt to reach the summit.
examples.cn: 他们尝试登顶，但未能成功。

examples.en: The plan proved abortive from the start.
examples.cn: 这个计划从一开始就注定失败。

sensesIntro.en: The senses grow from the literal image of a birth that does not happen, then spread to plans, revolts, efforts, medical treatment, and underdeveloped organs.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从「未能出生」的字面意象生长出来，再扩展到计划、起义、努力、医学治疗与发育不全的器官。

core.cn: 核心意象：一个在「出生」前就被截断的过程

branches.en: Attempts, plans, and efforts that produce no result.
branches.cn: 尝试、计划与努力没有产生结果。

branches.en: A revolt or coup that is crushed before it takes hold.
branches.cn: 起义或政变在站稳前被压碎。

branches.en: Medical processes stopped early, including the literal pregnancy sense.
branches.cn: 医学过程被早期截断，包括字面的妊娠义。

branches.en: An organ whose growth stops before it can function.
branches.cn: 器官在具备功能前停止生长。

branches.en: The general sense of any movement halting before its natural end.
branches.cn: 任何运动在自然结束前停下的普遍义。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem abort-, the adjective ending -ive, and the noun and verb endings around it.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 abort-、形容词后缀 -ive，以及周围的名词与动词后缀构成。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aboriri 与 abortus 是 abort 与 abortive 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其分词。

名词，义为「流产；中止」

definition_zh: 概念框架；研究者把相关概念及其关系组织起来、用以界定范围并指导分析的结构
definition_en: a researcher's organized map of the concepts relevant to a study and the relationships among them
core_image: 白板上画着一圈圈方框，每个框里写一个概念，箭头把彼此的关系连起来，最后收束成一个整体
scene: 做质性研究的学生把访谈里反复出现的几类现象先画成方框，再用箭头标出它们的关系。 The conceptual framework shows how the three factors influence one another.
sceneCN: 这里指用图示把概念与关系组织起来的框架（第 1 个义项：概念及其关系的组织图）；句意为这个概念框架显示了三个因素之间如何相互影响。

pos.zh: 概念框架；概念体系

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语「 conceive」而来的名词，义为「概念」
由「概念」加形容词尾构成，义为「概念的」
加动词尾，义为「概念化；把……形成概念」
再加表示行为的名词尾，义为「概念化过程」
加副词尾，义为「在概念上」

senses.title: A map of concepts and their links
senses.definition: a diagram or scheme that places the key concepts of a study and draws the links between them
senses.definitionCN: 把研究的关键概念摆出来并画出彼此关系的图式或方案
senses.example: The conceptual framework places trust between communication and cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把信任放在沟通与合作之间。
senses.why: A map is not the land, but it fixes which places connect, and the phrase does exactly that for ideas.
senses.whyCN: 地图不是土地，却固定了哪些地方相连，这个词组对观念做的正是这件事。

senses.title: The researcher's own synthesis
senses.definition: the arrangement the researcher builds from the literature rather than a scheme borrowed whole
senses.definitionCN: 研究者从文献中自行搭建的安排，而非整套搬用的方案
senses.example: Her conceptual framework grew out of five years of field notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的概念框架是从五年的田野笔记里长出来的。
senses.why: Theoretical frameworks are borrowed, but conceptual ones are assembled, which is why the possessive «her» matters.
senses.whyCN: 理论框架是借的，概念框架是拼的，所以这里用「她的」来限定。

senses.title: A diagram of the variables
senses.definition: a visual arrangement of variables and arrows that shows expected directions of influence
senses.definitionCN: 把变量与箭头排成图，显示预期的影响方向
senses.example: The conceptual framework puts the mediator in the middle of the diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把中介变量放在图示中央。
senses.why: Arrows carry direction, and a framework drawn with arrows reads almost like a claim about cause.
senses.whyCN: 箭头带方向，用箭头画出的框架读起来几乎就是对因果的主张。

senses.title: The set of constructs to be measured
senses.definition: the defined constructs that the study will turn into measures or interview codes
senses.definitionCN: 研究将转化为测量指标或访谈编码的、已界定的构念
senses.example: Each box in the conceptual framework became a scale in the questionnaire.
senses.exampleCN: 概念框架里的每个方框都变成了问卷中的一张量表。
senses.why: What is drawn must eventually be measured, so the framework also lists the constructs that need instruments.
senses.whyCN: 画出来的东西最终要能被测量，因此框架也列出需要工具去测的构念。

senses.title: The scheme for coding qualitative data
senses.definition: the analytic scheme that guides how interviews or observations are sorted into categories
senses.definitionCN: 指导如何把访谈或观察归入各类别的分析方案
senses.example: The coder used the conceptual framework to group the responses.
senses.exampleCN: 编码员用这个概念框架给回答分组。
senses.why: In qualitative work the framework becomes a set of boxes that the raw talk is sorted into.
senses.whyCN: 在质性研究里，框架变成一组方框，原始话语被分装进去。

senses.title: The stated scope of the study
senses.definition: the boundary that the framework draws around what the study will and will not examine
senses.definitionCN: 框架为研究划定考察与不考察范围的边界
senses.example: The conceptual framework excludes firms with fewer than ten staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把不足十人的企业排除在外。
senses.why: A frame has edges, and stating the concepts also states what is left outside them.
senses.whyCN: 框有边，界定概念的同时也界定了框外之物。

senses.title: The framework section of a proposal
senses.titleCN: 研究计划中的框架部分
senses.definition: the written part of a proposal that presents and justifies the concept map
senses.definitionCN: 研究计划中呈现并论证概念图的书面部分
senses.example: The conceptual framework takes four pages of the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 概念框架在研究计划里占了四页。
senses.why: A drawing needs a caption, and academic writing turns the drawing into a named section.
senses.whyCN: 图需要说明文字，学术写作便把这张图变成一个具名章节。

senses.title: A guide for programme design
senses.definition: the concept scheme used to plan a policy, service or intervention outside pure research
senses.definitionCN: 用于在纯研究之外规划政策、服务或干预的概念方案
senses.example: The agency adopted the conceptual framework when it redesigned the service.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构在重新设计服务时采用了这个概念框架。
senses.why: The same map that organizes research can organize action, because both need to know which factors connect.
senses.whyCN: 组织研究的那张图也能组织行动，因为两者都需要知道哪些因素相连。

intro.en: Conceptual framework joins a Latin word for a conceived idea with an English word for a supporting structure. It names the map a researcher builds before the measuring begins.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「被构想出的观念」的词，与英语中表示承重结构的词接在一起，指研究者在开始测量之前搭好的那张图。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and with the prefix com- it produced concipere, to take in and conceive.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「拿、抓」，加上表示「共同」的前缀后构成「收进、孕育」，即构想。

items.en: Conceptus named a taking in, hence a conceived idea; English concept arrived through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词指「收进」，因而指被构想出的观念；英语的「概念」经法语在十六世纪进入。

items.en: The adjective conceptual appeared in the seventeenth century for what exists in the mind rather than in the hand.
items.cn: 形容词「概念的」在十七世纪出现，指存在于头脑而非手中的东西。

items.en: Frame named a structure that gives shape and support, and its verb meant to construct.
items.cn: 这个词指给出形状与支撑的结构，其动词义为建造。

items.en: The compound appeared in the sixteenth or seventeenth century for a skeletal support; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十六或十七世纪出现，指骨架式的支撑；确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: Research methods texts fixed conceptual framework as the researcher's own map, distinct from a borrowed theoretical framework.
items.cn: 研究方法教材把「概念框架」固定为研究者自绘的图，与借用的「理论框架」相区别。

note.en: The first group belongs to the concept family or looks similar; the second group names neighbouring research structures.
note.cn: 第一组属于「概念」同族或形近；第二组指相邻的研究结构。

entries.definition: A general idea formed by taking the shared features of many cases.
entries.definitionCN: 指从众多事例的共同点中形成的一般观念。

entries.definition: Existing in thought or organized around concepts.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在于思想中或以概念组织的。

entries.definition: To form a concept of something or to describe it in conceptual terms.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物形成概念或以概念方式描述。

entries.definition: The act of forming an idea, or the idea formed.
entries.definitionCN: 指形成观念的行为或所形成的观念。

entries.definition: A supporting structure, physical or conceptual.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑结构，可为实物或概念。

entries.definition: To leave out; it looks like concept but comes from a taking-out prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指排除在外；形近但来自「取出」的前缀。

entries.definition: A theory structure borrowed from a field, which a study then applies.
entries.definitionCN: 指从某一领域借来、由研究加以应用的理论结构。

entries.definition: The structure that shows how a problem will be broken into analysable parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示如何把问题拆成可分析部分的结构。

entries.definition: A simplified formal representation of variables and their paths.
entries.definitionCN: 指变量及其路径的简化形式表示。

entries.definition: A field-wide way of thinking, broader than a single study's map.
entries.definitionCN: 指领域层面的整套思维方式，比单项研究的图更宽。

entries.definition: A defined attribute that a study intends to measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究打算测量的、已界定的属性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the whiteboard picture, the real distinction from a theoretical framework, and the measurement link.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用白板画图的画面、与理论框架的真实区别，以及通向测量的一环。

normal.en: Concept gives the boxes; framework gives the arrows and the edges.
normal.cn: 概念提供方框，框架提供箭头与边界。

normal.en: Conceptual frameworks are built, not borrowed, which is why they belong to a named researcher.
normal.cn: 概念框架是搭建的而非借用的，所以它属于某个具体研究者。

normal.en: Every box on the board should later become a measure, a code or a hypothesis.
normal.cn: 板上的每个方框后来都该变成一项测量、一个编码或一条假设。

normal.en: The theoretical framework supplies the theory; the conceptual framework supplies the arrangement.
normal.cn: 理论框架提供理论，概念框架提供排列方式。

normal.en: A map with arrows already whispers a claim about which way influence runs.
normal.cn: 带箭头的图已经在暗示影响朝哪个方向流动。

abstract.en: A conceptual framework is a promise that everything drawn will eventually be either measured or explained.
abstract.cn: 概念框架是一份承诺：画出的每样东西最终要么被测量，要么被解释。

abstract.en: Two researchers can share the same theory and still draw different maps, which shows the map is the person.
abstract.cn: 两位研究者可以共用一套理论却画出不同的图，说明图就是人本身。

abstract.en: The frame is drawn before the evidence arrives, and that order is what makes it a frame rather than a summary.
abstract.cn: 框架在证据到来之前就画好，正是这个顺序使它成为框架而不是总结。

examples.en: The conceptual framework groups motivation, opportunity and ability under one scheme.
examples.cn: 这个概念框架把动机、机会与能力归入同一套方案。

examples.en: She revised the conceptual framework after the first round of interviews.
examples.cn: 第一轮访谈之后，她修订了概念框架。

examples.en: The diagram in the conceptual framework became the basis for the questionnaire.
examples.cn: 概念框架中的图示成了问卷设计的基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「概念」是框里的字，「框架」是框本身：把概念装进框、用箭头连起来，就是概念框架

root: 「概念」源自拉丁语 concipere「收进、孕育」，其词根为 capere「抓取」；「框架」由古英语 framian「有用、推进」与 work 合成。二十世纪研究方法文献把「概念框架」固定为研究者自绘的概念关系图。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the map itself to its practical uses: the concept map, the researcher's synthesis, the variable diagram, the constructs to measure, the coding scheme, the scope, the proposal section, and the design guide.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从图本身走向实际用途：概念关系图、研究者的综合、变量图示、待测构念、编码方案、研究范围、计划章节、设计指南。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boxes are drawn on a board and arrows are added until the separate ideas read as one structure.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上先画方框，再补箭头，直到分开的观念读起来像一个整体。

branches.en: THE BUILT MAP: concepts placed and linked by the researcher's own synthesis.
branches.cn: 搭建的图：由研究者自行综合摆放并连接的概念。

branches.en: THE ARROWED DIAGRAM: variables arranged with expected directions of influence.
branches.cn: 带箭头的图：变量按预期影响方向排列。

branches.en: THE MEASURABLE SIDE: constructs turned into scales and codes.
branches.cn: 可测量的一面：构念转化为量表与编码。

branches.en: THE STATED EDGES: the scope that is drawn and then written into the proposal.
branches.cn: 明示的边缘：画出范围，再写进研究计划。

branches.en: THE OUTWARD USE: the same map guiding a service or policy design.
branches.cn: 向外的用途：同一张图指导服务或政策设计。

intro.en: Conceptual framework joins a Latin idea word to an Old English structure word; both halves keep their original pictures.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的观念词与古英语的结构词接起来，两半都保留着原始画面。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies concipere and conceptus; the structure half is native English and has no Latin entry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「构想」与「概念」两词；结构那一半是英语本族词，没有拉丁语条目。

items.example: It turns taking into taking in.
items.exampleCN: 它把「拿」变成「收进来」。

items.example: The root behind concept and capture.
items.exampleCN: 这是「概念」与「捕获」共同的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the idea word.
items.exampleCN: 这是观念词的直接来源。

items.example: It became English concept.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「概念」。

items.example: It forms conceptual from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由名词构成形容词「概念的」。

items.example: The load-bearing half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是词组里承重的那一半。

items.example: It joins frame to make framework.
items.exampleCN: 它与「框」合成「框架」。

items.example: The verb built on the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是由该形容词构成的动词。

definition_zh: 新陈代谢；生物体内全部化学变化的总和；物质与能量的转化
definition_en: the whole set of chemical reactions by which a living organism converts substances and energy, keeping itself running
core_image: 一条环形的流水线在同一个身体里转圈，一端拆开原料，另一端拼出新件，中间不断放热
scene: 这里指「新陈代谢」。 A hibernating animal slows its metabolism so that one stored fat reserve lasts the whole winter.
sceneCN: 这里 metabolism 指「代谢整体、代谢速率」（第 1 个义项：体内全部化学变化的总和及其运行强度）；冬眠动物让它放慢，一份脂肪储备就能撑过整个冬天。图中可辨识物件：环形流水线、拆解的原料、拼出的新件、散出的热。

pos.zh: 新陈代谢；代谢（不可数；指不同生物或不同个体的代谢体系时可用复数 metabolisms）

derivatives.zh: 代谢的
代谢；分解
代谢产物
代谢组学
分解代谢
合成代谢

senses.title: The whole chemical turnover
senses.titleCN: 新陈代谢：体内全部化学变化的总和
senses.definition: the entire set of chemical reactions that keep an organism alive
senses.definitionCN: 维持生物体存活所需的全部化学反应
senses.example: Metabolism includes both the burning of fuel and the building of new tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 新陈代谢既包括燃烧燃料，也包括构建新组织。
senses.why: Greek metabolē meant 'a change, a turning over'; physiology took the word for the constant change inside a body, so the name starts as change itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 metabolē 意为「变化、翻转」；生理学用它指体内持续发生的更换，因此这个名字的起点就是「变化」。

senses.title: Materials passing through
senses.titleCN: 物质代谢：原料的进出与转化
senses.definition: the material side of that turnover, the conversion of substances into other substances
senses.definitionCN: 这一周转的物质面：一种物质被转化为另一种物质
senses.example: Protein metabolism decides how much nitrogen the body keeps.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质代谢决定身体保留多少氮。
senses.why: because the change is chemical, the word also names the material side of the turnover, not only its energy side.
senses.whyCN: 由于变化是化学性的，这个词也命名周转的物质面，而不只是能量面。

senses.title: Energy in and out
senses.definition: the energy side of the turnover, the release of energy from fuel and its use for work
senses.definitionCN: 周转的能量面：从燃料释放能量并用于做功
senses.example: Energy metabolism converts food into heat and movement.
senses.exampleCN: 能量代谢把食物转化为热与运动。
senses.why: the same loop can be read as a budget of energy, so the word covers calories as well as molecules.
senses.whyCN: 同一条环路也可以读成能量预算，因此这个词同时覆盖分子与卡路里。

senses.title: The idle rate
senses.titleCN: 基础代谢：静息时的最低消耗
senses.definition: the rate of turnover while at rest, measured as basal metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 静息状态下的周转速率，即基础代谢
senses.example: Basal metabolism accounts for most of the calories a sedentary adult burns.
senses.exampleCN: 基础代谢占久坐成年人消耗热量的绝大部分。
senses.why: once measured in the clinic, the word also names a rate, the speed of the loop rather than its contents.
senses.whyCN: 当它在临床被测定后，这个词也命名一个速率，即环路的快慢而非内容。

senses.title: The tearing-down half
senses.definition: the breaking-down half of the turnover, catabolism, which releases energy
senses.definitionCN: 周转中拆解并释放能量的那一半，即分解代谢
senses.example: Catabolism breaks glucose into carbon dioxide and water.
senses.exampleCN: 分解代谢把葡萄糖拆成二氧化碳和水。
senses.why: the loop has two halves, and the tearing side is one of them; the word as a whole can name that half.
senses.whyCN: 环路有两半，拆解的一侧是其中之一；作为一个整体，这个词也可指那一半。

senses.title: The building half
senses.definition: the building half of the turnover, anabolism, which consumes energy
senses.definitionCN: 周转中拼装并消耗能量的那一半，即合成代谢
senses.example: Anabolism uses ATP to assemble amino acids into muscle.
senses.exampleCN: 合成代谢用 ATP 把氨基酸组装成肌肉。
senses.why: because the same loop both breaks and builds, the whole word can stand for the constructing half as well.
senses.whyCN: 由于同一条环路既拆又建，整个词也可指构建的那一半。

senses.title: What the body does to a drug
senses.titleCN: 药物代谢：体内对药物的改造
senses.definition: the chemical alteration of drugs and other foreign compounds inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 药物及其他外来化合物在体内被化学改造的过程
senses.example: A fast metabolism clears the drug before the next dose is due.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢快的人在下一次给药前就把药清除掉了。
senses.why: pharmacology applies the loop to foreign molecules, so the word also names detoxification rather than nourishment.
senses.whyCN: 药理学把这条环路用于外来分子，因此这个词也命名解毒过程，而不是营养过程。

senses.title: The map of all routes
senses.titleCN: 代谢网络：全部通路的集合
senses.definition: the network of all the pathways taken together, studied as a system
senses.definitionCN: 把全部通路作为一个系统来研究的网络
senses.example: Systems biology draws the whole metabolism as a map of arrows.
senses.exampleCN: 系统生物学把整个代谢画成一张箭头地图。
senses.why: when the single loop is scaled up, it becomes a network; the singular word then names the map rather than a reaction.
senses.whyCN: 当单一环路被放大，它就成了网络；单数形式此时命名的是那张地图，而不是某一反应。

intro.en: Metabolism comes from Greek metabolē 'a change, a turning over', built on meta- 'over, beyond' and ballein 'to throw'. English first used it for change in general.
intro.cn: metabolism 出自希腊 metabolē「变化、翻转」，由 meta-「越过」与 ballein「投掷」构成。英语最初用它泛指变化。

items.en: metabolē named a change or a turning over, including a change of government. The base is a Greek noun of action, not a Latin one.
items.cn: metabolē 指变化或翻转，也包括政权的更替。其词基是希腊动作名词，不是拉丁语。

items.en: ballein 'to throw' supplies the second element; meta- adds the idea of change of place or state. The deeper origin of ballein is not settled.
items.cn: ballein「投掷」提供第二个构件；meta- 加入位置或状态改变的意思。ballein 的更深来源并无定论。

items.en: English metabolism appears in the seventeenth century for change in general; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 metabolism 于 17 世纪出现，泛指变化；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology narrowed the word to the chemical turnover of a living body, the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学把该词收窄为活体内的化学周转，即今天主导的义项。

items.en: Twentieth-century biochemistry split the loop into catabolism and anabolism and mapped the pathways as a network.
items.cn: 20 世纪生物化学把环路分成分解代谢与合成代谢，并把它绘成通路网络。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): ballein has no agreed pre-Greek source, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction; the earliest English date is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ballein 在希腊语之前的来源并无共识，其背后的印欧形式属重构；英语最早书证年代亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that share meta- but not always the same root; group two holds the two halves and the neighbouring processes.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 meta- 但未必同源的形近词；第二组是这一过程的两半以及相邻过程。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of metabolism'; it qualifies rate, pathway or disease but does not name the whole turnover.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「代谢的」；修饰速率、通路或疾病，但不命名整个周转过程。

entries.definition: The spread of cancer, from Greek meta- 'beyond' plus stasis 'standing'. It shares the prefix and not the root, so it is not a relative of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指癌症的转移，由希腊 meta-「越过」加 stasis「站立」构成；只共享前缀而词根不同，因此与 metabolism 并非同族。

entries.definition: A substance produced or consumed during metabolism; it is an item in the loop, not the loop.
entries.definitionCN: 指代谢过程中产生或消耗的物质；是环路中的一项，而不是环路。

entries.definition: A figure of speech, from meta- 'over' plus pherein 'to carry'. Another meta- word with an unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 一种修辞，由 meta-「越过」加 pherein「搬运」构成；又一个前缀相同而词根无关的词。

entries.definition: The set of reactions that break molecules down and release energy; it is one half of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指拆解分子并释放能量的一组反应；是代谢的一半。

entries.definition: The set of reactions that build molecules and consume energy; the other half of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指构建分子并消耗能量的一组反应；是代谢的另一半。

entries.definition: The process by which cells obtain energy from fuel, usually with oxygen; it is a major route inside metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞从燃料获取能量、通常需氧的过程；是代谢内部的主干路线。

entries.definition: The breakdown of food before it enters the body's chemistry; digestion precedes most metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指食物进入体内化学之前的分解；消化先于大部分代谢。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: meta- 'over' + ballein 'to throw': a constant throwing over, change itself.
normal.cn: meta-「越过」+ ballein「投掷」：不停翻来覆去地更换，也就是「变化」本身。

normal.en: The family runs metabolism, metabolic, metabolize, metabolite, metabolomics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 metabolism、metabolic、metabolize、metabolite、metabolomics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: basal metabolism, energy metabolism, lipid metabolism, drug metabolism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：基础代谢、能量代谢、脂质代谢、药物代谢。

normal.en: The loop has two halves: catabolism tears down, anabolism builds up.
normal.cn: 环路有两半：分解代谢拆，合成代谢建。

normal.en: A slow metabolism is a rate, not a substance; do not confuse it with a metabolite.
normal.cn: 「代谢慢」说的是速率，不是物质；别与代谢产物混为一谈。

abstract.en: Picture a loop of conveyor belts that never stop, tearing and joining at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一条不停的环形传送带，一边拆一边接。

abstract.en: Picture a stove that both burns wood and builds furniture from the same pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一座炉子，同一堆木料既用来烧，也用来做家具。

abstract.en: Picture an accounting book where income and spending are kept in one column.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，收入与支出记在同一栏里。

examples.en: Regular exercise raises resting metabolism for several hours.
examples.cn: 规律运动会提高数小时的静息代谢。

examples.en: The liver handles most drug metabolism in the body.
examples.cn: 体内大部分药物代谢由肝脏承担。

examples.en: Metabolism in a dormant seed nearly stops until water returns.
examples.cn: 休眠种子在水分回来之前代谢几乎停止。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「每天（meta）都在烧（bal）」——身体里不停拆与建的化学周转 → 新陈代谢

root: 希腊 metabolē「变化、翻转」（meta-「越过」+ ballein「投掷」）→ 英语 metabolism；19 世纪收窄为体内化学周转。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a loop keeps turning inside a body, and that turning is read as the whole turnover, as materials, as energy, as a resting rate, as the tearing half, as the building half, as drug clearing, and as a map of all routes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：身体里的一条环路不停转动，这次转动依次被读成整体周转、物质、能量、静息速率、拆解的一半、构建的一半、药物清除，以及全部路线的地图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed loop that tears materials apart at one end and joins new ones at the other, shedding heat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条闭环，一端拆开材料，另一端拼出新物，同时散出热。

branches.en: THE WHOLE LOOP: the turnover as such, the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 整条环路：周转本身，最朴素的义项。

branches.en: TWO LEDGERS: the same loop read as material flow and as energy flow.
branches.cn: 两本账：同一条环路被读成物质流与能量流。

branches.en: SPEED: at rest the loop has a measurable idle rate.
branches.cn: 速度：静息时环路有一个可测的怠速。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: tearing down and building up, each able to stand for the whole.
branches.cn: 两半：拆解与构建，各自都能代指整体。

branches.en: FOREIGN MATTER AND MAP: clearing drugs, and drawing every route as one network.
branches.cn: 外来物与地图：清除药物，并把所有路线绘成一张网络。

intro.en: Metabolism is a Greek compound behind a Latinized ending -ismus; the English family adds Latin -ic and -ita and Greek -omics.
intro.cn: metabolism 是拉丁化词尾 -ismus 包裹的希腊合成词；英语词族另加拉丁 -ic、-ita 与希腊 -omics。

latinIntro.en: No inherited Latin base exists. New Latin metabolismus is a Latinized spelling; the -ismus ending reached English through Latin and French.
latinIntro.cn: 没有传承的拉丁词基。新拉丁语 metabolismus 是拉丁化拼写；-ismus 词尾经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.meaning: the turnover of a living body
items.example: Metabolism slows during fasting.
items.exampleCN: 禁食期间代谢变慢。

items.example: Metabolic rate rises with fever.
items.exampleCN: 发热时代谢率升高。

items.meaning: to subject a substance to metabolism
items.example: The liver metabolizes most drugs.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏代谢大多数药物。

items.meaning: a substance made or used in metabolism
items.meaningCN: 代谢中生成或消耗的物质
items.example: Lactate is a metabolite of glucose.
items.exampleCN: 乳酸是葡萄糖的一种代谢产物。

items.example: Metabolomics compares hundreds of small molecules.
items.exampleCN: 代谢组学比较数百种小分子。

items.example: Catabolism releases energy from fat.
items.exampleCN: 分解代谢从脂肪中释放能量。

items.example: Anabolism requires energy and building blocks.
items.exampleCN: 合成代谢需要能量与构建单元。

items.meaning: a person or organ that metabolizes
items.example: Fast metabolizers clear caffeine quickly.
items.exampleCN: 快代谢型的人清除咖啡因很快。

items.example: Basal metabolism is measured after sleep.
items.exampleCN: 基础代谢在睡眠后测定。
